# Yinshi Cross-Cutting Architecture Report

Scope: `backend/src/yinshi` (Python/FastAPI), `frontend/src` (React/Vite), `desktop/src` (Electron/TypeScript), `sidecar/src` (Node). Vendored and build directories excluded.

---

## 1. Noise IK / encryption protocol: no single authoritative definition

There is no shared schema, no IDL, and no generated artifact. The wire protocol is re-derived independently in Python and TypeScript, with matching literal constants written twice.

### 1a. Noise handshake layer (duplicated constants)

| Constant | Backend | Frontend |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Protocol name `Noise_IK_25519_ChaChaPoly_SHA256` | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise.py:22` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:8` |
| Max message length 65535 | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise.py:26` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:11` |
| IK first message overhead 96 | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise.py:24` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:12` |
| IK second message minimum 48 | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise.py:25` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:13` |
| Rehandshake threshold 1048576 | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise_session.py:24` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:14` and `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:398` |
| X25519 key length 32 | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise.py:23` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:9` |
| Prologue / protocol tag `yinshi-runner-v1` | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise_session.py:23` and `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_capabilities.py:27` | `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:9`, applied at `:411` |

The two implementations also use different crypto stacks: Python `noiseprotocol` plus `cryptography` (`runner_noise.py:11-20`), browser `@richardhopton/noise-c.wasm` (`noiseIk.ts:1-6`). Behavior parity is maintained only by hand.

### 1b. Capability token layer

Issued and verified only in Python: `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_capabilities.py:161-306` (Ed25519-signed claims: `scopes`, `token_id`, `transfer_id`, `expires_at`, `max_frame_bytes`, `max_session_bytes`, `initiator_public_key`, `protocol`). Consumed by the runner responder in `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise_session.py:178-225`, which sends the handshake response payload `{"protocol":..., "transfer_id":...}` at `:216-224`. The frontend independently re-validates the same claim shape in `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:14-25` (`RunnerCapabilityResponse`) and `:118-...` (`validateCapability`), and parses the handshake reply at `:449-452`.

### 1c. Relay framing layer (16-byte UUID prefix)

- Hosted relay adds prefix on client-to-runner: `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_relay.py:266-283` (`uuid.UUID(transfer_id).bytes + ciphertext`).
- Hosted relay strips prefix on runner-to-client: `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_relay.py:298-330`.
- Runner side parses and re-adds the same prefix: `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_agent_relay.py:96-116`.
- Control messages are hand-built JSON strings, not models: `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_relay.py:262-263` and `:328-330` emit `'{"transfer_id":"..","type":"close"}'`; parsed at `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_agent_relay.py:77-95,129-156`.
- The browser never sees the prefix. It sends bare ciphertext and expects the literal readiness string `'{"type":"ready"}'`: `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:441-443`.

### 1d. RPC envelope layer (v2 / v1 mismatch)

- Frontend request envelope keys and version: `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:472-484` sends `v: 2`.
- Backend accepted key set is named `_REQUEST_KEYS_V1` and lacks `query`: `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:17`, version and type checks at `:83-100`.
- Response envelope built at `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:313-325`, parsed independently at `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:495-500` (`parseRpcResponse`).
- Size limits diverge by construction: browser caps a request at 49152 bytes (`encryptedRunnerClient.ts:487-488`); backend caps the frame from the capability (`runner_noise_session.py:265-271`); relay caps at `_RELAY_FRAME_BYTES_MAX` (`runner_relay.py:271`).

Risk: the version literal is `2` on the wire while the backend constant is named `_REQUEST_KEYS_V1`, and `query` appears in the frontend envelope but not in the backend key allowlist. Confirm this is intentional before changing either side.

### 1e. Desktop encryption is a separate, unrelated scheme

`desktop/src/runtimeSecrets.ts:6-11` defines `RuntimeSecrets {version:1, secretKey, encryptionPepper, keyEncryptionKey}` and hands those to the Python helper. The backend consumes the same values through settings and derives keys with its own AES-GCM helpers: `backend/src/yinshi/services/crypto.py:48-231` and `backend/src/yinshi/services/control_encryption.py:11-30`. `desktop/src/diskEncryption.ts` is only FileVault status detection (`detectFileVaultStatus`, imported at `desktop/src/main.ts:29`); it is not part of the Noise protocol.

### Files requiring coordinated edit for any Noise/wire protocol change

1. `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise.py` (handshake primitives, protocol name, length bounds)
2. `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise_session.py` (prologue, capability binding, handshake reply payload, frame limits)
3. `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_capabilities.py` (protocol tag, claim schema, scope set)
4. `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py` (RPC envelope, version, route-to-scope table)
5. `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_relay.py` (UUID prefix framing, control JSON, byte limits)
6. `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_agent_relay.py` (runner-side demux, prefix, control JSON)
7. `backend/src/yinshi/api/runner_relay.py` (WebSocket endpoints)
8. `backend/src/yinshi/api/runners.py` (capability issuance response; protocol echoed at `:198`)
9. `backend/src/yinshi/runner_agent.py` (relay client, registration, key pinning)
10. `backend/src/yinshi/models.py` (`RunnerCapabilityCreateIn:370`, `RunnerCapabilityOut:393`, `RunnerRegisterIn:324`, `RunnerNoiseKeyConfirmationIn:360`)
11. `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts` (browser handshake, constants)
12. `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts` (prologue, capability validation, RPC envelope, ready string)
13. `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts` (scope selection, session byte budget at `:92`)
14. `frontend/src/runtime/encryptedUpload.ts` (chunked upload over the same channel)
15. `frontend/src/runner/repositories.ts` (BYOC listing path)
16. `frontend/src/types/noise-c-wasm.d.ts` (wasm binding types)
17. Test mirrors: `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.test.ts`, `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.test.ts`, and the backend test suite for the five services above.

Desktop is not on this list unless `desktop/src/hostedApiGateway.ts` route allowlist has to change (see section 3).

---

## 2. Type and schema duplication

There is no OpenAPI codegen. `frontend/package.json` contains no `openapi` or generate script. The backend only serves `/openapi.json` when `debug` is true (`backend/src/yinshi/main.py:451`). Every API shape is hand-written twice.

Duplicated pairs (Pydantic in `backend/src/yinshi/models.py`, TypeScript in `frontend/src/api/client.ts`):

| Shape | Backend | Frontend |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Repo | `models.py:136` `RepoOut` | `client.ts:1` `Repo` |
| Workspace | `models.py:163` `WorkspaceOut` | `client.ts:178` `Workspace` |
| Session | `models.py:212` `SessionOut` | `client.ts:189` `SessionInfo` |
| Message | `models.py:224` `MessageOut` | `client.ts:199` `Message` |
| CloudRunner | `models.py:294` `CloudRunnerOut` | `client.ts:83` `CloudRunner` |
| Runner registration | `models.py:314` `CloudRunnerRegistrationOut` | `client.ts:101` `CloudRunnerRegistration` |
| Runner capability | `models.py:393` `RunnerCapabilityOut` | `encryptedRunnerClient.ts:14` `RunnerCapabilityResponse` |
| Runner capability request | `models.py:370` `RunnerCapabilityCreateIn` | `encryptedRunnerClient.ts:27` `RunnerCapabilityRequest` |
| Provider descriptor | `models.py:448` `ProviderDescriptorOut` | `client.ts:34` `ProviderDescriptor` |
| Provider setup field | `models.py:439` `ProviderSetupFieldOut` | `client.ts:27` `ProviderSetupField` |
| Model descriptor | `models.py:460` `ModelDescriptorOut` | `client.ts:47` `ModelDescriptor` |
| Provider catalog | `models.py:475` `ProviderCatalogOut` | `client.ts:60` `ProviderCatalog` |

| Provider connection | `models.py:602` `ProviderConnectionOut` | `client.ts:66` `ProviderConnection` |
| API key | `models.py:625` `ApiKeyOut` | `client.ts:19` `ApiKey` |
| Pi config | `models.py:672` `PiConfigOut` | `client.ts:131` `PiConfig` |
| Pi command | `models.py:687` `PiCommand` | `client.ts:146` `PiCommand` |
| Pi config commands | `models.py:702` `PiConfigCommandsOut` | `client.ts:153` `PiConfigCommands` |
| Pi package release | `models.py:713` `PiPackageReleaseOut` | `client.ts:157` `PiPackageRelease` |
| Pi release notes | `models.py:724` `PiReleaseNotesOut` | `client.ts:166` `PiReleaseNotes` |
| Prompt request | `models.py:237` `WSPrompt` | inline in `frontend/src/runtime/promptStream.ts:42-49` and `client.ts:514-522` |

Additional non-`models.py` duplications:
- Terminal channel shapes: `backend/src/yinshi/api/terminal_channels.py:36-61` (`TerminalStartRequest`, `TerminalStartResponse`, `TerminalInputRequest`, `TerminalResizeRequest`, `TerminalEventBatchResponse`) versus `frontend/src/runtime/terminalChannel.ts:11-59` (hand validators for the same fields, and event-type set at `:4-9`).
- Prompt run shapes: `backend/src/yinshi/api/prompt_runs.py:99-160` versus `frontend/src/runtime/promptStream.ts:30-40` (`PromptRunResponse`, `PromptEventBatchResponse`) and the status enum duplicated at `promptStream.ts:9-28`.
- SSE event union: `frontend/src/api/client.ts:453-502` (`SSEEvent`, `ContentBlock`, `normalizeEvent`) mirrors sidecar output shaping in `sidecar/src/sidecar.js:244-250`.
- Desktop IPC contract: `desktop/src/desktopApi.ts` (`DESKTOP_IPC_CHANNELS`, `HostedApiRequest`) duplicated for the renderer in `frontend/src/types/desktop.d.ts`.
- Runtime secrets contract: `desktop/src/runtimeSecrets.ts:6-11` versus backend settings fields consumed in `backend/src/yinshi/config.py` and `services/crypto.py`.

---

## 3. Runtime abstraction: where "which runtime" is decided (key finding)

There are two orthogonal runtime axes, and they are not unified.

**Axis A - frontend `RuntimeRef.location`**: `local` | `hosted` | `byoc`. Defined at `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:10-17`, unresolved variant at `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeRef.ts:6-13`.

**Axis B - backend `AppMode`**: `desktop` | `hosted` | `worker`. Selected in `backend/src/yinshi/main.py:415-457` (`create_app(mode=...)`).

These names do not line up: frontend `local` maps to backend `desktop` mode, frontend `byoc` maps to backend `worker` mode running inside `runner_agent`, frontend `hosted` maps to backend `hosted` mode. Nothing enforces the mapping.

### Decision points, exhaustive

**Frontend (13 sites)**

1. `frontend/src/runtime/useRuntimeResource.ts:42-51` - primary resolution: parse encoded ID, resolve ref, build transport. This is the canonical entry.
2. `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeRef.ts:62-67` - `defaultRuntimeRef` picks `local` when `desktop` is true, otherwise `hosted`.
3. `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeRef.ts:69-83` - `runtimeResourceId` encodes the runtime into the URL (`hosted.`, `local.`, `byoc.<b64url>.`).
4. `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeRef.ts:87-119` - `parseRuntimeResourceId` decodes it back.
5. `frontend/src/runtime/resolveRuntime.ts:20-45` - resolves BYOC by fetching `/api/settings/runner` and requires `noise_key_confirmed`.
6. `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:259-273` - `createRuntimeTransport` picks `hostedApi` versus `api` based on `location === "hosted" && window.yinshiDesktop !== undefined`.
7. `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:286-296` - request dispatch branches to the encrypted Noise path for `byoc`.
8. `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:322-340` - upload branches three ways (`byoc` encrypted, hosted-in-desktop bridge, plain multipart).
9. `frontend/src/runtime/promptStream.ts:174` - poll delay differs by runtime location.
10. `frontend/src/api/client.ts:321-325, 374-378, 402-410` - independent bridge routing by hard-coded path set `DESKTOP_HOSTED_RUNNER_PATHS`, bypassing `RuntimeRef` entirely.
11. `frontend/src/api/piCommandsCache.ts:22` - cache key namespacing by runtime.
12. `frontend/src/components/Sidebar.tsx:172-247, 269, 514, 973, 1096, 1132, 1161` - runtime discovery and aggregation across all three locations; also builds the default runtime a second time at `:172-174` instead of calling `defaultRuntimeRef`.
13. `frontend/src/pages/Settings.tsx:604-606, 631-638, 697, 716, 757-764` - a third open-coded copy of the same default-runtime rule at `:604-606` and `:697`.

Duplication: the "desktop implies local, otherwise hosted" rule is written in three places (`runtimeRef.ts:62-67`, `Sidebar.tsx:172-174`, `Settings.tsx:604-606, 697`).

**Backend (mode branches)**

14. `backend/src/yinshi/main.py:415-424` - `create_app` validates the mode.
15. `backend/src/yinshi/main.py:309-322` - worker mode gets a distinct middleware stack and returns early.
16. `backend/src/yinshi/main.py:344-352` - desktop mode injects `DesktopTenantMiddleware` with the fixed `desktop-local` tenant.
17. `backend/src/yinshi/main.py:361-363` - desktop mode uses a different CSP.
18. `backend/src/yinshi/main.py:379-412` - `_include_routes` splits `execution_routers` from `control_routers`; only `hosted` gets the control plane (auth, runners, relay, GitHub, desktop devices).
19. `backend/src/yinshi/main.py:266` - hosted-only startup work.
20. `backend/src/yinshi/runner_worker.py:264-293` - the runner agent constructs `create_app(mode="worker", ...)` in-process.
21. `backend/src/yinshi/worker_runtime.py:29-40` - `WorkerHttpDispatcher` asserts `app.state.mode == "worker"` and dispatches via ASGI with no socket.

### The triplicated route-to-scope/allowlist table

The same URL surface is enumerated three times, in three languages, with three different purposes:

- `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:132-215` - authoritative server-side scope enforcement.
- `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:46-206` - client-side scope selection for capability requests.
- `desktop/src/hostedApiGateway.ts:16-170` - Electron bridge allowlist.

Any new API route needs edits in all three, plus the FastAPI router. Divergence here is a security-relevant defect class, not just churn.

  preload.ts -> desktopApi (IPC channel names) -> exposes window.yinshiDesktop

  sidecarSupervisor -> spawns sidecar/src/index.js over SIDECAR_SOCKET_PATH

backend/src/yinshi
  main.py -> api/* routers, middleware, config, db
  api/stream.py, api/prompt_runs.py -> services/prompt_journal -> services/sidecar
  api/terminal_channels.py -> services/terminal_journal -> sidecar socket

  api/runners.py -> services/{runners, runner_capabilities, runner_relay}
  api/runner_relay.py -> services/runner_relay
  runner_agent.py -> services/runner_agent_relay -> services/runner_rpc
                                                 -> services/runner_noise_session
                                                 -> services/runner_noise
                  -> runner_worker.py -> main.create_app(mode="worker")
                                      -> worker_runtime.WorkerHttpDispatcher
  services/control_encryption -> services/crypto

sidecar/src
  index.js -> sidecar.js -> git_auth.js, git_askpass_client.js, constants.js

```

### Circular and surprising dependencies

1. **Import cycle, broken by a deferred import.** `runner_worker.py:264` does `from yinshi.main import create_app` inside a method body. `main.py` transitively reaches worker code through routers and `worker_auth`. The cycle is real; only the function-local import keeps it working.
2. **The backend imports itself over a network boundary.** The BYOC runner runs a full second FastAPI app in-process (`runner_worker.py:288`) and calls it through ASGI without a listening socket (`worker_runtime.py`). One codebase acts as both control plane and remote worker, distinguished only by `app.state.mode`.
3. **Route knowledge is triplicated across three languages** (section 3). This is the highest-risk coupling in the repository.
4. **Two terminal subsystems and two agent-stream subsystems coexist**, each with its own framing. `api/terminals.py` (WebSocket) and `api/terminal_channels.py` (polling) both talk to the same sidecar with separately written newline-JSON helpers.
5. **`api/client.ts` bypasses the runtime abstraction.** `DESKTOP_HOSTED_RUNNER_PATHS` (`client.ts:321-325`) hard-codes three paths that must go over the Electron bridge, independent of `RuntimeRef`. A fourth control-plane path added later will silently take the wrong transport.
6. **The default-runtime rule is written three times** (`runtimeRef.ts:62-67`, `Sidebar.tsx:172-174`, `Settings.tsx:604-606` and `:697`).
7. **Terminology drift**: frontend `local`/`hosted`/`byoc` versus backend `desktop`/`hosted`/`worker` versus deployment terms "runner"/"sidecar"/"helper". No file states the mapping.
8. **The sidecar is the only fully decoupled component.** It knows nothing about runtimes, tenants, or Noise. It is a good extraction boundary.

---

## Start Here

Open `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts` first. Lines 10-17 define the `RuntimeRef` union that drives every frontend branch, lines 46-206 hold the route-to-scope table duplicated in `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:132-215` and `desktop/src/hostedApiGateway.ts:16-170`, and lines 259-340 contain the dispatch that selects plain HTTP, the Electron bridge, or the Noise channel. Then read `backend/src/yinshi/main.py:379-412` for the backend mode split.

4. Is `client.ts:streamPrompt` (SSE) still live, or superseded by `promptStream.ts`? `useAgentStream.ts:127` still falls back to it when no runtime transport is present.

## 1. Noise IK / encryption protocol: no single authoritative definition

There is no shared schema, no IDL, and no generated artifact. The wire protocol is re-derived independently in Python and TypeScript, with matching literal constants written twice.

### 1a. Noise handshake layer (duplicated constants)

| Constant | Backend | Frontend |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Protocol name `Noise_IK_25519_ChaChaPoly_SHA256` | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise.py:22` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:8` |
| Max message length 65535 | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise.py:26` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:11` |
| IK first message overhead 96 | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise.py:24` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:12` |
| IK second message minimum 48 | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise.py:25` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:13` |
| Rehandshake threshold 1048576 | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise_session.py:24` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:14` and `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:398` |
| X25519 key length 32 | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise.py:23` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:9` |
| Prologue / protocol tag `yinshi-runner-v1` | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise_session.py:23` and `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_capabilities.py:27` | `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:9`, applied at `:411` |

The two implementations also use different crypto stacks: Python `noiseprotocol` plus `cryptography` (`runner_noise.py:11-20`), browser `@richardhopton/noise-c.wasm` (`noiseIk.ts:1-6`). Behavior parity is maintained only by hand.

### 1b. Capability token layer

Issued and verified only in Python: `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_capabilities.py:161-306` (Ed25519-signed claims: `scopes`, `token_id`, `transfer_id`, `expires_at`, `max_frame_bytes`, `max_session_bytes`, `initiator_public_key`, `protocol`). Consumed by the runner responder in `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise_session.py:178-225`, which sends the handshake response payload `{"protocol":..., "transfer_id":...}` at `:216-224`. The frontend independently re-validates the same claim shape in `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:14-25` (`RunnerCapabilityResponse`) and `:118-...` (`validateCapability`), and parses the handshake reply at `:449-452`.

### 1c. Relay framing layer (16-byte UUID prefix)

- Hosted relay adds prefix on client-to-runner: `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_relay.py:266-283` (`uuid.UUID(transfer_id).bytes + ciphertext`).
- Hosted relay strips prefix on runner-to-client: `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_relay.py:298-330`.
- Runner side parses and re-adds the same prefix: `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_agent_relay.py:96-116`.
- Control messages are hand-built JSON strings, not models: `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_relay.py:262-263` and `:328-330` emit `'{"transfer_id":"..","type":"close"}'`; parsed at `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_agent_relay.py:77-95,129-156`.
- The browser never sees the prefix. It sends bare ciphertext and expects the literal readiness string `'{"type":"ready"}'`: `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:441-443`.

### 1d. RPC envelope layer (v2 / v1 mismatch)

- Frontend request envelope keys and version: `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:472-484` sends `v: 2`.
- Backend accepted key set is named `_REQUEST_KEYS_V1` and lacks `query`: `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:17`, version and type checks at `:83-100`.
- Response envelope built at `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:313-325`, parsed independently at `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:495-500` (`parseRpcResponse`).
- Size limits diverge by construction: browser caps a request at 49152 bytes (`encryptedRunnerClient.ts:487-488`); backend caps the frame from the capability (`runner_noise_session.py:265-271`); relay caps at `_RELAY_FRAME_BYTES_MAX` (`runner_relay.py:271`).

Risk: the version literal is `2` on the wire while the backend constant is named `_REQUEST_KEYS_V1`, and `query` appears in the frontend envelope but not in the backend key allowlist. Confirm this is intentional before changing either side.

### 1e. Desktop encryption is a separate, unrelated scheme

`desktop/src/runtimeSecrets.ts:6-11` defines `RuntimeSecrets {version:1, secretKey, encryptionPepper, keyEncryptionKey}` and hands those to the Python helper. The backend consumes the same values through settings and derives keys with its own AES-GCM helpers: `backend/src/yinshi/services/crypto.py:48-231` and `backend/src/yinshi/services/control_encryption.py:11-30`. `desktop/src/diskEncryption.ts` is only FileVault status detection (`detectFileVaultStatus`, imported at `desktop/src/main.ts:29`); it is not part of the Noise protocol.

## 3. Runtime abstraction: where "which runtime" is decided (key finding)

There are two orthogonal runtime axes, and they are not unified.

**Axis A - frontend `RuntimeRef.location`**: `local` | `hosted` | `byoc`. Defined at `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:10-17`, unresolved variant at `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeRef.ts:6-13`.

**Axis B - backend `AppMode`**: `desktop` | `hosted` | `worker`. Selected in `backend/src/yinshi/main.py:415-457` (`create_app(mode=...)`).

These names do not line up: frontend `local` maps to backend `desktop` mode, frontend `byoc` maps to backend `worker` mode running inside `runner_agent`, frontend `hosted` maps to backend `hosted` mode. Nothing enforces the mapping.

**Frontend (13 sites)**

1. `frontend/src/runtime/useRuntimeResource.ts:42-51` - primary resolution: parse encoded ID, resolve ref, build transport. This is the canonical entry.
2. `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeRef.ts:62-67` - `defaultRuntimeRef` picks `local` when `desktop` is true, otherwise `hosted`.
3. `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeRef.ts:69-83` - `runtimeResourceId` encodes the runtime into the URL (`hosted.`, `local.`, `byoc.<b64url>.`).
4. `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeRef.ts:87-119` - `parseRuntimeResourceId` decodes it back.
5. `frontend/src/runtime/resolveRuntime.ts:20-45` - resolves BYOC by fetching `/api/settings/runner` and requires `noise_key_confirmed`.
6. `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:259-273` - `createRuntimeTransport` picks `hostedApi` versus `api` based on `location === "hosted" && window.yinshiDesktop !== undefined`.
7. `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:286-296` - request dispatch branches to the encrypted Noise path for `byoc`.
8. `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:322-340` - upload branches three ways (`byoc` encrypted, hosted-in-desktop bridge, plain multipart).
9. `frontend/src/runtime/promptStream.ts:174` - poll delay differs by runtime location.
10. `frontend/src/api/client.ts:321-325, 374-378, 402-410` - independent bridge routing by hard-coded path set `DESKTOP_HOSTED_RUNNER_PATHS`, bypassing `RuntimeRef` entirely.
11. `frontend/src/api/piCommandsCache.ts:22` - cache key namespacing by runtime.
12. `frontend/src/components/Sidebar.tsx:172-247, 269, 514, 973, 1096, 1132, 1161` - runtime discovery and aggregation across all three locations; also builds the default runtime a second time at `:172-174` instead of calling `defaultRuntimeRef`.
13. `frontend/src/pages/Settings.tsx:604-606, 631-638, 697, 716, 757-764` - a third open-coded copy of the same default-runtime rule at `:604-606` and `:697`.

Duplication: the "desktop implies local, otherwise hosted" rule is written in three places (`runtimeRef.ts:62-67`, `Sidebar.tsx:172-174`, `Settings.tsx:604-606, 697`).

**Backend (mode branches)**

14. `backend/src/yinshi/main.py:415-424` - `create_app` validates the mode.
15. `backend/src/yinshi/main.py:309-322` - worker mode gets a distinct middleware stack and returns early.
16. `backend/src/yinshi/main.py:344-352` - desktop mode injects `DesktopTenantMiddleware` with the fixed `desktop-local` tenant.
17. `backend/src/yinshi/main.py:361-363` - desktop mode uses a different CSP.
18. `backend/src/yinshi/main.py:379-412` - `_include_routes` splits `execution_routers` from `control_routers`; only `hosted` gets the control plane (auth, runners, relay, GitHub, desktop devices).
19. `backend/src/yinshi/main.py:266` - hosted-only startup work.
20. `backend/src/yinshi/runner_worker.py:264-293` - the runner agent constructs `create_app(mode="worker", ...)` in-process.
21. `backend/src/yinshi/worker_runtime.py:29-40` - `WorkerHttpDispatcher` asserts `app.state.mode == "worker"` and dispatches via ASGI with no socket.
22. `backend/src/yinshi/api/terminal_channels.py:97-105` - execution-time branch: if the sidecar context has no socket path, fall back to the settings socket and the host workspace path; otherwise remap the path into the container.
23. `backend/src/yinshi/services/sidecar_runtime.py:30-38` - `TenantSidecarContext` with nullable `socket_path` is the mechanism for that branch (containerized versus local sidecar).
24. `backend/src/yinshi/api/terminals.py:188-274` - a separate desktop terminal WebSocket proxy path (`_run_desktop_terminal_proxy`), parallel to the polling channel API.
25. `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:132-215` - route-to-scope table that gates what a BYOC runtime may execute.

**Desktop (Electron)**

26. `desktop/src/main.ts:369` and `desktop/src/runtimeLaunchConfig.ts:120-160` - decides helper and sidecar socket paths and env for the local runtime.
27. `desktop/src/localRuntime.ts:15-30` - asserts helper and sidecar agree on `SIDECAR_SOCKET_PATH`; starts the local runtime pair.
28. `desktop/src/hostedApiGateway.ts:16-170` - decides which hosted API routes the renderer may reach through the bridge. This is a third copy of the route table.
29. `desktop/src/helperSupervisor.ts` and `desktop/src/sidecarSupervisor.ts` (imported at `desktop/src/main.ts:32,48`) - process lifecycle for the local runtime.

**Sidecar (Node)**

30. `sidecar/src/sidecar.js:937` - socket path from `SIDECAR_SOCKET_PATH`, default `/tmp/yinshi-...`.
31. `sidecar/src/sidecar.js:946` - `SIDECAR_LOAD_DOTENV === "1"` toggles dotenv loading; desktop sets it to `"0"` at `desktop/src/runtimeLaunchConfig.ts:158`.
32. `sidecar/src/sidecar.js:1154-1210` - single message-type dispatch table; the sidecar itself is runtime-agnostic and has no notion of hosted versus local.

### The triplicated route-to-scope/allowlist table

The same URL surface is enumerated three times, in three languages, with three different purposes:

- `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:132-215` - authoritative server-side scope enforcement.
- `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:46-206` - client-side scope selection for capability requests.
- `desktop/src/hostedApiGateway.ts:16-170` - Electron bridge allowlist.

Any new API route needs edits in all three, plus the FastAPI router. Divergence here is a security-relevant defect class, not just churn.

---

## 4. Terminal and agent-stream data paths

### Terminal path A: polling channel (BYOC and general runtime transport)

1. `frontend/src/runtime/terminalChannel.ts:82-...` - `openRuntimeTerminal` POSTs `/api/workspaces/{id}/terminals`, then polls `/events/{sequence}`; validates event types at `:4-9,47-59`.
2. `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:286-296` - for BYOC, wraps each call in a Noise RPC.
3. `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:441-520` - handshake plus encrypted request.
4. `backend/src/yinshi/api/runner_relay.py` then `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_relay.py:266-330` - UUID-prefixed relay.
5. `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_agent_relay.py:96-116` - demux to the per-transfer session.
6. `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:71-325` - envelope parse, scope check, response build.
7. `backend/src/yinshi/worker_runtime.py:29-...` - ASGI dispatch into the worker app.
8. `backend/src/yinshi/api/terminal_channels.py:121-250` - terminal routes.
9. `backend/src/yinshi/api/terminal_channels.py:79-110` - resolves workspace paths and the sidecar socket, branching on `runtime.socket_path is None`.
10. `backend/src/yinshi/services/terminal_journal.py:85-512` - newline-delimited JSON to the sidecar socket, buffers output into sequenced batches (`_append_event:404`, `_split_terminal_data:439`, `_decode_message:512`).
11. `sidecar/src/sidecar.js:1184-1210` - dispatch of `terminal_attach`, `terminal_input`, `terminal_resize`, `terminal_restart`, `terminal_kill`, `terminal_detach`.
12. `sidecar/src/sidecar.js:982-1082` - `pty.spawn`, `onData` emits `terminal_data` (`:999-1003`), `onExit` emits `terminal_exit` (`:1005-1012`), ready emits `terminal_ready` (`:1036-1042`).

### Terminal path B: direct WebSocket proxy (desktop/hosted)

`backend/src/yinshi/api/terminals.py:273-274` exposes `/api/workspaces/{id}/terminal` as a WebSocket, with its own sidecar framing helpers `_send_sidecar:72`, `_read_sidecar:81`, `_proxy_browser_to_sidecar:92`, `_proxy_sidecar_to_browser:169`, `_run_desktop_terminal_proxy:188`, and workspace resolution in `backend/src/yinshi/services/desktop_terminal.py:37`.

Reimplemented logic: sidecar newline-JSON framing exists twice in the backend (`terminals.py:72-91` and `terminal_journal.py:478-512`). Terminal event validation exists in Python (`terminal_journal.py:404-454`) and again in TypeScript (`terminalChannel.ts:47-59`). Terminal size bounds 2..500 exist in `terminal_channels.py:37-38,49-51` and `terminalChannel.ts:38-45`.

### Agent stream path A: SSE (direct hosted/desktop)

1. `frontend/src/hooks/useAgentStream.ts:127-133` calls `streamPrompt`.
2. `frontend/src/api/client.ts:514-570` - `fetch` POST to `/api/sessions/{id}/prompt`, manual SSE line splitting at `:551-566`, `normalizeEvent` at `:503-512`.
3. `backend/src/yinshi/api/stream.py:771-773` - `prompt_session`, execution context resolved at `:630`.
4. `backend/src/yinshi/services/sidecar.py:39-136` - newline-JSON transport to the sidecar with an 8 MiB message limit.
5. `sidecar/src/sidecar.js:1203-1209` - `query` / `resolve` / `cancel` dispatch; content block shaping at `:244-250`.

### Agent stream path B: polled run journal (runtime transport, required for BYOC)

1. `frontend/src/hooks/useAgentStream.ts:114-126` calls `startRuntimePrompt`.
2. `frontend/src/runtime/promptStream.ts:30-249` - POST `/runs`, poll `/runs/{id}/events/{seq}`, POST `/cancel`; reuses `normalizeEvent` from `client.ts`.
3. `backend/src/yinshi/api/prompt_runs.py:99-160`.
4. `backend/src/yinshi/services/prompt_journal.py:89-515` - run lifecycle, sequenced event batches, `_default_prompt_executor:58` bridging to the same sidecar execution used by the SSE path.
5. Same sidecar hops as path A.

Reimplemented logic across the two agent-stream paths: event normalization is shared, but transport, status enums, cancellation, and terminal-status handling are written twice (`client.ts:514-575` versus `promptStream.ts:9-249`). Two independent journals exist with near-identical sequenced-batch semantics: `prompt_journal.py` and `terminal_journal.py`.

---

## 5. Component dependency map

```
frontend/src
  App.tsx -> pages/{Session,Settings,Landing,Login}, components/Sidebar
  pages/Session.tsx -> runtime/useRuntimeResource -> runtime/{runtimeRef,resolveRuntime,runtimeTransport}
  runtime/runtimeTransport.ts -> api/client (api, hostedApi)
                              -> runner/encryptedRunnerClient
                              -> runtime/encryptedUpload
  runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts -> crypto/noiseIk -> noise-c.wasm
                                  -> api/client (capability issuance)
  hooks/useAgentStream.ts -> api/client.streamPrompt  (SSE path)
                          -> runtime/promptStream     (polled path)
  components/Sidebar.tsx -> runtime/*, runner/repositories, api/client
  api/client.ts -> window.yinshiDesktop (types/desktop.d.ts)

desktop/src
  main.ts -> appController, helperSupervisor, sidecarSupervisor, localRuntime,
             runtimeLaunchConfig, runtimeSecrets, credentialStore, diskEncryption,
             hostedApiGateway, hostedAccessSession, hostedAuth, security, shellPolicy,
             authCallbackListener, localRepositoryImport, automaticUpdates, desktopApi
  preload.ts -> desktopApi (IPC channel names) -> exposes window.yinshiDesktop
  helperSupervisor -> spawns backend `create_app(mode="desktop")` via desktop_runtime.py
  sidecarSupervisor -> spawns sidecar/src/index.js over SIDECAR_SOCKET_PATH

backend/src/yinshi
  main.py -> api/* routers, middleware, config, db
  api/stream.py, api/prompt_runs.py -> services/prompt_journal -> services/sidecar
  api/terminal_channels.py -> services/terminal_journal -> sidecar socket
  api/terminals.py -> services/desktop_terminal -> sidecar socket   (parallel WS path)
  api/terminal_channels.py -> services/{workspace_runtime_paths, sidecar_runtime, container}
  api/runners.py -> services/{runners, runner_capabilities, runner_relay}
  api/runner_relay.py -> services/runner_relay
  runner_agent.py -> services/runner_agent_relay -> services/runner_rpc
                                                 -> services/runner_noise_session
                                                 -> services/runner_noise
                  -> runner_worker.py -> main.create_app(mode="worker")
                                      -> worker_runtime.WorkerHttpDispatcher
  services/control_encryption -> services/crypto

sidecar/src
  index.js -> sidecar.js -> git_auth.js, git_askpass_client.js, constants.js
  no dependency on backend, frontend, or desktop
```

### Circular and surprising dependencies

1. **Import cycle, broken by a deferred import.** `runner_worker.py:264` does `from yinshi.main import create_app` inside a method body. `main.py` transitively reaches worker code through routers and `worker_auth`. The cycle is real; only the function-local import keeps it working.
2. **The backend imports itself over a network boundary.** The BYOC runner runs a full second FastAPI app in-process (`runner_worker.py:288`) and calls it through ASGI without a listening socket (`worker_runtime.py`). One codebase acts as both control plane and remote worker, distinguished only by `app.state.mode`.
3. **Route knowledge is triplicated across three languages** (section 3). This is the highest-risk coupling in the repository.
4. **Two terminal subsystems and two agent-stream subsystems coexist**, each with its own framing. `api/terminals.py` (WebSocket) and `api/terminal_channels.py` (polling) both talk to the same sidecar with separately written newline-JSON helpers.
5. **`api/client.ts` bypasses the runtime abstraction.** `DESKTOP_HOSTED_RUNNER_PATHS` (`client.ts:321-325`) hard-codes three paths that must go over the Electron bridge, independent of `RuntimeRef`. A fourth control-plane path added later will silently take the wrong transport.
6. **The default-runtime rule is written three times** (`runtimeRef.ts:62-67`, `Sidebar.tsx:172-174`, `Settings.tsx:604-606` and `:697`).
7. **Terminology drift**: frontend `local`/`hosted`/`byoc` versus backend `desktop`/`hosted`/`worker` versus deployment terms "runner"/"sidecar"/"helper". No file states the mapping.
8. **The sidecar is the only fully decoupled component.** It knows nothing about runtimes, tenants, or Noise. It is a good extraction boundary.

---

## Start Here

Open `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts` first. Lines 10-17 define the `RuntimeRef` union that drives every frontend branch, lines 46-206 hold the route-to-scope table duplicated in `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:132-215` and `desktop/src/hostedApiGateway.ts:16-170`, and lines 259-340 contain the dispatch that selects plain HTTP, the Electron bridge, or the Noise channel. Then read `backend/src/yinshi/main.py:379-412` for the backend mode split.

## Open questions

1. Is the RPC envelope `v: 2` (`encryptedRunnerClient.ts:483`) versus `_REQUEST_KEYS_V1` (`runner_rpc.py:17`) intentional?
2. Does the backend accept the `query` key that the frontend always sends? It is absent from `_REQUEST_KEYS_V1`.
3. Is `api/terminals.py` (WebSocket) still live, or superseded by `api/terminal_channels.py` (polling)? Both are registered in `main.py:395-396`.
4. Is `client.ts:streamPrompt` (SSE) still live, or superseded by `promptStream.ts`? `useAgentStream.ts:127` still falls back to it when no runtime transport is present.

# Yinshi Cross-Cutting Architecture Report

Scope: `backend/src/yinshi` (Python/FastAPI), `frontend/src` (React/Vite), `desktop/src` (Electron/TypeScript), `sidecar/src` (Node). Vendored and build directories excluded.

---

## 1. Noise IK / encryption protocol: no single authoritative definition

There is no shared schema, no IDL, and no generated artifact. The wire protocol is re-derived independently in Python and TypeScript, with matching literal constants written twice.

### 1a. Noise handshake layer (duplicated constants)

| Constant | Backend | Frontend |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Protocol name `Noise_IK_25519_ChaChaPoly_SHA256` | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise.py:22` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:8` |
| Max message length 65535 | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise.py:26` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:11` |
| IK first message overhead 96 | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise.py:24` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:12` |
| IK second message minimum 48 | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise.py:25` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:13` |
| Rehandshake threshold 1048576 | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise_session.py:24` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:14`, `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:398` |
| X25519 key length 32 | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise.py:23` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:9` |
| Prologue / protocol tag `yinshi-runner-v1` | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise_session.py:23`, `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_capabilities.py:27` | `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:9`, applied at `:411` |

The two implementations use different crypto stacks: Python `noiseprotocol` plus `cryptography` (`runner_noise.py:11-20`), browser `@richardhopton/noise-c.wasm` (`noiseIk.ts:1-6`). Parity is maintained only by hand.

### 1b. Capability token layer

Issued and verified only in Python: `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_capabilities.py:161-306` (Ed25519-signed claims: `scopes`, `token_id`, `transfer_id`, `expires_at`, `max_frame_bytes`, `max_session_bytes`, `initiator_public_key`, `protocol`). Consumed by the runner responder in `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise_session.py:178-225`, which sends the handshake response payload `{"protocol":..., "transfer_id":...}` at `:216-224`. The frontend independently re-validates the same claim shape in `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:14-25` (`RunnerCapabilityResponse`) and in `validateCapability` at `:118`, and parses the handshake reply at `:449-452`.

### 1c. Relay framing layer (16-byte UUID prefix)

- Hosted relay adds the prefix on client-to-runner: `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_relay.py:266-283` (`uuid.UUID(transfer_id).bytes + ciphertext`).
- Hosted relay strips the prefix on runner-to-client: `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_relay.py:298-330`.
- Runner side parses and re-adds the same prefix: `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_agent_relay.py:96-116`.
- Control messages are hand-built JSON strings, not models: `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_relay.py:262-263` and `:328-330` emit `'{"transfer_id":"..","type":"close"}'`; parsed at `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_agent_relay.py:77-95,129-156`.
- The browser never sees the prefix. It sends bare ciphertext and expects the literal readiness string `'{"type":"ready"}'`: `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:441-443`.

### 1d. RPC envelope layer (version mismatch)

- Frontend request envelope keys and version: `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:472-484` sends `v: 2`.
- Backend accepted key set is named `_REQUEST_KEYS_V1` and lacks `query`: `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:17`, version and type checks at `:83-100`.
- Response envelope built at `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:313-325`, parsed independently at `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:495-500`.
- Size limits diverge by construction: browser caps a request at 49152 bytes (`encryptedRunnerClient.ts:487-488`); the responder caps the frame from the capability (`runner_noise_session.py:265-271`); the relay caps at `_RELAY_FRAME_BYTES_MAX` (`runner_relay.py:271`).

Risk: the version literal is `2` on the wire while the backend constant is named `_REQUEST_KEYS_V1`, and `query` appears in the frontend envelope but not in the backend key allowlist.

### 1e. Desktop encryption is a separate, unrelated scheme

`desktop/src/runtimeSecrets.ts:6-11` defines `RuntimeSecrets {version:1, secretKey, encryptionPepper, keyEncryptionKey}` and passes those to the Python helper. The backend consumes the same values through settings and derives keys with its own AES-GCM helpers: `backend/src/yinshi/services/crypto.py:48-231` and `backend/src/yinshi/services/control_encryption.py:11-30`. `desktop/src/diskEncryption.ts` is only FileVault status detection (`detectFileVaultStatus`, imported at `desktop/src/main.ts:29`); it is not part of the Noise protocol.

### Files requiring coordinated edit for any Noise or wire protocol change

1. `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise.py` (handshake primitives, protocol name, length bounds)
2. `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise_session.py` (prologue, capability binding, handshake reply, frame limits)
3. `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_capabilities.py` (protocol tag, claim schema, scope set)
4. `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py` (RPC envelope, version, route-to-scope table)
5. `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_relay.py` (UUID prefix framing, control JSON, byte limits)
6. `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_agent_relay.py` (runner-side demux, prefix, control JSON)
7. `backend/src/yinshi/api/runner_relay.py` (WebSocket endpoints)
8. `backend/src/yinshi/api/runners.py` (capability issuance; protocol echoed at `:198`)
9. `backend/src/yinshi/runner_agent.py` (relay client, registration, key pinning)
10. `backend/src/yinshi/models.py` (`RunnerCapabilityCreateIn:370`, `RunnerCapabilityOut:393`, `RunnerRegisterIn:324`, `RunnerNoiseKeyConfirmationIn:360`)
11. `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts` (browser handshake, constants)
12. `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts` (prologue, capability validation, RPC envelope, ready string)
13. `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts` (scope selection, session byte budget at `:92`)
14. `frontend/src/runtime/encryptedUpload.ts` (chunked upload over the same channel)
15. `frontend/src/runner/repositories.ts` (BYOC listing path)
16. `frontend/src/types/noise-c-wasm.d.ts` (wasm binding types)
17. Test mirrors: `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.test.ts`, `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.test.ts`, plus the backend tests for the five services above.

Desktop is not on this list unless the `desktop/src/hostedApiGateway.ts` route allowlist must change (see section 3).

---

## 2. Type and schema duplication

There is no OpenAPI codegen. `frontend/package.json` has no `openapi` or generate script. The backend serves `/openapi.json` only when `debug` is true (`backend/src/yinshi/main.py:451`). Every API shape is hand-written twice.

Duplicated pairs (Pydantic in `backend/src/yinshi/models.py`, TypeScript in `frontend/src/api/client.ts`):

| Shape | Backend | Frontend |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Repo | `models.py:136` `RepoOut` | `client.ts:1` `Repo` |
| Workspace | `models.py:163` `WorkspaceOut` | `client.ts:178` `Workspace` |
| Session | `models.py:212` `SessionOut` | `client.ts:189` `SessionInfo` |
| Message | `models.py:224` `MessageOut` | `client.ts:199` `Message` |
| CloudRunner | `models.py:294` `CloudRunnerOut` | `client.ts:83` `CloudRunner` |
| Runner registration | `models.py:314` `CloudRunnerRegistrationOut` | `client.ts:101` `CloudRunnerRegistration` |
| Runner capability response | `models.py:393` `RunnerCapabilityOut` | `encryptedRunnerClient.ts:14` `RunnerCapabilityResponse` |
| Runner capability request | `models.py:370` `RunnerCapabilityCreateIn` | `encryptedRunnerClient.ts:27` `RunnerCapabilityRequest` |
| Provider descriptor | `models.py:448` | `client.ts:34` |
| Provider setup field | `models.py:439` | `client.ts:27` |
| Model descriptor | `models.py:460` | `client.ts:47` |
| Provider catalog | `models.py:475` | `client.ts:60` |
| Provider auth start | `models.py:483` | `client.ts:109` |
| Provider auth status | `models.py:495` | `client.ts:119` |
| Provider connection | `models.py:602` | `client.ts:66` |
| API key | `models.py:625` | `client.ts:19` |
| Pi config | `models.py:672` | `client.ts:131` |
| Pi command | `models.py:687` | `client.ts:146` |
| Pi config commands | `models.py:702` | `client.ts:153` |
| Pi package release | `models.py:713` | `client.ts:157` |
| Pi release notes | `models.py:724` | `client.ts:166` |
| Prompt request | `models.py:237` `WSPrompt` | inline at `frontend/src/runtime/promptStream.ts:42-49` and `client.ts:514-522` |

Additional duplications outside `models.py`:

- Terminal channel shapes: `backend/src/yinshi/api/terminal_channels.py:36-61` versus hand validators in `frontend/src/runtime/terminalChannel.ts:11-59`, with the event-type set at `:4-9`.
- Prompt run shapes: `backend/src/yinshi/api/prompt_runs.py:99-160` versus `frontend/src/runtime/promptStream.ts:30-40`; the run status enum is duplicated at `promptStream.ts:9-28`.
- SSE event union: `frontend/src/api/client.ts:453-502` mirrors sidecar content shaping at `sidecar/src/sidecar.js:244-250`.
- Desktop IPC contract: `desktop/src/desktopApi.ts` duplicated for the renderer in `frontend/src/types/desktop.d.ts`.
- Runtime secrets contract: `desktop/src/runtimeSecrets.ts:6-11` versus backend settings consumed by `backend/src/yinshi/config.py` and `services/crypto.py`.

---

## 3. Runtime abstraction: where the runtime decision is made (key finding)

Two orthogonal runtime axes exist, and they are not unified.

Axis A, frontend `RuntimeRef.location`: `local`, `hosted`, `byoc`. Defined at `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:10-17`; unresolved variant at `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeRef.ts:6-13`.

Axis B, backend `AppMode`: `desktop`, `hosted`, `worker`. Selected in `backend/src/yinshi/main.py:415-457` through `create_app(mode=...)`.

The names do not line up. Frontend `local` maps to backend `desktop`, frontend `byoc` maps to backend `worker` inside `runner_agent`, frontend `hosted` maps to backend `hosted`. Nothing in the code states or enforces that mapping.

### Decision points, exhaustive

Frontend, 13 sites:

1. `frontend/src/runtime/useRuntimeResource.ts:42-51` - canonical resolution: parse encoded ID, resolve the ref, build the transport.
2. `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeRef.ts:62-67` - `defaultRuntimeRef` returns `local` on desktop, otherwise `hosted`.
3. `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeRef.ts:69-83` - `runtimeResourceId` encodes the runtime into the URL (`hosted.`, `local.`, `byoc.<b64url>.`).
4. `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeRef.ts:87-119` - `parseRuntimeResourceId` decodes it.
5. `frontend/src/runtime/resolveRuntime.ts:20-45` - resolves BYOC by fetching `/api/settings/runner`, requiring `noise_key_confirmed`.
6. `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:259-273` - selects `hostedApi` versus `api` when `location === "hosted" && window.yinshiDesktop !== undefined`.
7. `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:286-296` - dispatches `byoc` requests through the encrypted Noise channel.
8. `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:322-340` - upload branches three ways: BYOC encrypted, hosted-in-desktop bridge, plain multipart.
9. `frontend/src/runtime/promptStream.ts:174` - poll delay differs by runtime location.
10. `frontend/src/api/client.ts:321-325, 374-378, 402-410` - independent bridge routing keyed on the hard-coded `DESKTOP_HOSTED_RUNNER_PATHS` set, bypassing `RuntimeRef`.
11. `frontend/src/api/piCommandsCache.ts:22` - cache key namespaced by runtime.
12. `frontend/src/components/Sidebar.tsx:172-247, 269, 514, 973, 1096, 1132, 1161` - runtime discovery and aggregation across all three locations; rebuilds the default runtime at `:172-174` instead of calling `defaultRuntimeRef`.
13. `frontend/src/pages/Settings.tsx:604-606, 631-638, 697, 716, 757-764` - a third open-coded copy of the default-runtime rule at `:604-606` and `:697`.

Backend, mode branches:

14. `backend/src/yinshi/main.py:415-424` - `create_app` validates the mode.

- `App.tsx` depends on `pages/{Session,Settings,Landing,Login}` and `components/Sidebar`.

- `api/stream.py` and `api/prompt_runs.py` depend on `services/prompt_journal`, which depends on `services/sidecar`.
- `api/terminal_channels.py` depends on `services/terminal_journal`, `services/workspace_runtime_paths`, `services/sidecar_runtime`, `services/container`.
- `api/terminals.py` depends on `services/desktop_terminal` and talks to the sidecar socket directly.
- `api/runners.py` depends on `services/runners`, `services/runner_capabilities`, `services/runner_relay`.
- `runner_agent.py` depends on `services/runner_agent_relay`, which depends on `services/runner_rpc`, `services/runner_noise_session`, `services/runner_noise`; it also depends on `runner_worker.py`, which imports `main.create_app` and `worker_runtime.WorkerHttpDispatcher`.

### Circular and surprising dependencies

1. Import cycle broken by a deferred import. `backend/src/yinshi/runner_worker.py:264` does `from yinshi.main import create_app` inside a method body, while `main.py` reaches worker code through routers and `worker_auth`. The cycle is real; only the function-local import keeps it working.
2. The backend imports itself across a network boundary. The BYOC runner runs a second full FastAPI app in-process (`runner_worker.py:288`) and calls it over ASGI with no listening socket (`worker_runtime.py`). One codebase is both control plane and remote worker, separated only by `app.state.mode`.
3. Route knowledge is triplicated across three languages (section 3). Highest-risk coupling in the repository.
4. Two terminal subsystems and two agent-stream subsystems coexist, each with its own framing. `api/terminals.py` (WebSocket) and `api/terminal_channels.py` (polling) both talk to the same sidecar through separately written newline-JSON helpers.
5. `api/client.ts` bypasses the runtime abstraction. `DESKTOP_HOSTED_RUNNER_PATHS` at `client.ts:321-325` hard-codes three paths that must use the Electron bridge, independent of `RuntimeRef`. A fourth control-plane path added later would silently take the wrong transport.
6. The default-runtime rule is written three times: `runtimeRef.ts:62-67`, `Sidebar.tsx:172-174`, `Settings.tsx:604-606` and `:697`.
7. Terminology drift: frontend `local`/`hosted`/`byoc`, backend `desktop`/`hosted`/`worker`, deployment terms runner, sidecar, helper. No file records the mapping.
8. The sidecar is the only fully decoupled component. It knows nothing about runtimes, tenants, or Noise, and is a clean extraction boundary.

## 1. Noise IK / encryption protocol: no single authoritative definition

There is no shared schema, no IDL, and no generated artifact. The wire protocol is re-derived independently in Python and TypeScript, with matching literal constants written twice.

### 1a. Noise handshake layer (duplicated constants)

| Constant | Backend | Frontend |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Protocol name `Noise_IK_25519_ChaChaPoly_SHA256` | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise.py:22` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:8` |
| Max message length 65535 | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise.py:26` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:11` |
| IK first message overhead 96 | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise.py:24` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:12` |
| IK second message minimum 48 | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise.py:25` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:13` |
| Rehandshake threshold 1048576 | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise_session.py:24` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:14`, `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:398` |
| X25519 key length 32 | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise.py:23` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:9` |
| Prologue / protocol tag `yinshi-runner-v1` | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise_session.py:23`, `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_capabilities.py:27` | `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:9`, applied at `:411` |

The two implementations use different crypto stacks: Python `noiseprotocol` plus `cryptography` (`runner_noise.py:11-20`), browser `@richardhopton/noise-c.wasm` (`noiseIk.ts:1-6`). Parity is maintained only by hand.

### 1b. Capability token layer

Issued and verified only in Python: `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_capabilities.py:161-306` (Ed25519-signed claims: `scopes`, `token_id`, `transfer_id`, `expires_at`, `max_frame_bytes`, `max_session_bytes`, `initiator_public_key`, `protocol`). Consumed by the runner responder in `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise_session.py:178-225`, which sends the handshake response payload `{"protocol":..., "transfer_id":...}` at `:216-224`. The frontend independently re-validates the same claim shape in `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:14-25` (`RunnerCapabilityResponse`) and in `validateCapability` at `:118`, and parses the handshake reply at `:449-452`.

### 1c. Relay framing layer (16-byte UUID prefix)

- Hosted relay adds the prefix on client-to-runner: `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_relay.py:266-283` (`uuid.UUID(transfer_id).bytes + ciphertext`).
- Hosted relay strips the prefix on runner-to-client: `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_relay.py:298-330`.
- Runner side parses and re-adds the same prefix: `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_agent_relay.py:96-116`.
- Control messages are hand-built JSON strings, not models: `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_relay.py:262-263` and `:328-330` emit `'{"transfer_id":"..","type":"close"}'`; parsed at `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_agent_relay.py:77-95,129-156`.
- The browser never sees the prefix. It sends bare ciphertext and expects the literal readiness string `'{"type":"ready"}'`: `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:441-443`.

### 1d. RPC envelope layer (version mismatch)

- Frontend request envelope keys and version: `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:472-484` sends `v: 2`.
- Backend accepted key set is named `_REQUEST_KEYS_V1` and lacks `query`: `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:17`, version and type checks at `:83-100`.
- Response envelope built at `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:313-325`, parsed independently at `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:495-500`.
- Size limits diverge by construction: browser caps a request at 49152 bytes (`encryptedRunnerClient.ts:487-488`); the responder caps the frame from the capability (`runner_noise_session.py:265-271`); the relay caps at `_RELAY_FRAME_BYTES_MAX` (`runner_relay.py:271`).

Risk: the version literal is `2` on the wire while the backend constant is named `_REQUEST_KEYS_V1`, and `query` appears in the frontend envelope but not in the backend key allowlist.

### 1e. Desktop encryption is a separate, unrelated scheme

`desktop/src/runtimeSecrets.ts:6-11` defines `RuntimeSecrets {version:1, secretKey, encryptionPepper, keyEncryptionKey}` and passes those to the Python helper. The backend consumes the same values through settings and derives keys with its own AES-GCM helpers: `backend/src/yinshi/services/crypto.py:48-231` and `backend/src/yinshi/services/control_encryption.py:11-30`. `desktop/src/diskEncryption.ts` is only FileVault status detection (`detectFileVaultStatus`, imported at `desktop/src/main.ts:29`); it is not part of the Noise protocol.

18. `backend/src/yinshi/main.py:379-412` - `_include_routes` splits execution routers from control routers; only `hosted` receives auth, runners, relay, GitHub, and desktop devices.
19. `backend/src/yinshi/main.py:266` - hosted-only startup work.
20. `backend/src/yinshi/runner_worker.py:264-293` - the runner agent builds `create_app(mode="worker", ...)` in-process.
21. `backend/src/yinshi/worker_runtime.py:29-40` - `WorkerHttpDispatcher` asserts `app.state.mode == "worker"` and dispatches over ASGI with no socket.
22. `backend/src/yinshi/api/terminal_channels.py:97-105` - execution-time branch: with no sidecar socket path, use the settings socket and the host workspace path; otherwise remap the path into the container.
23. `backend/src/yinshi/services/sidecar_runtime.py:30-38` - `TenantSidecarContext` with a nullable `socket_path` is the mechanism behind that branch.
24. `backend/src/yinshi/api/terminals.py:188-274` - a separate desktop terminal WebSocket proxy, parallel to the polling channel API.
25. `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:132-215` - route-to-scope table gating what a BYOC runtime may execute.

Desktop:

26. `desktop/src/main.ts:369` and `desktop/src/runtimeLaunchConfig.ts:120-160` - helper and sidecar socket paths plus environment for the local runtime.
27. `desktop/src/localRuntime.ts:15-30` - asserts helper and sidecar agree on `SIDECAR_SOCKET_PATH`, then starts the pair.
28. `desktop/src/hostedApiGateway.ts:16-170` - allowlist of hosted API routes reachable through the bridge. Third copy of the route table.
29. `desktop/src/helperSupervisor.ts` and `desktop/src/sidecarSupervisor.ts`, imported at `desktop/src/main.ts:32,48` - local runtime process lifecycle.

Sidecar:

30. `sidecar/src/sidecar.js:937` - socket path from `SIDECAR_SOCKET_PATH`.
31. `sidecar/src/sidecar.js:946` - `SIDECAR_LOAD_DOTENV === "1"` toggles dotenv; desktop sets `"0"` at `desktop/src/runtimeLaunchConfig.ts:158`.
32. `sidecar/src/sidecar.js:1154-1210` - one message-type dispatch table. The sidecar is runtime-agnostic and has no hosted versus local concept.

### Triplicated route-to-scope and allowlist table

The same URL surface is enumerated three times, in three languages, for three purposes:

- `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:132-215` - authoritative server-side scope enforcement.
- `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:46-206` - client-side scope selection for capability requests.
- `desktop/src/hostedApiGateway.ts:16-170` - Electron bridge allowlist.

Any new API route requires edits in all three plus the FastAPI router. Divergence here is a security-relevant defect class.

---

## 4. Terminal and agent-stream data paths

### Terminal path A: polling channel (used by the runtime transport, required for BYOC)

1. `frontend/src/runtime/terminalChannel.ts:82` - `openRuntimeTerminal` POSTs `/api/workspaces/{id}/terminals`, then polls `/events/{sequence}`; event validation at `:4-9,47-59`.
2. `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:286-296` - wraps each BYOC call in a Noise RPC.
3. `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:441-520` - handshake plus encrypted request.
4. `backend/src/yinshi/api/runner_relay.py` then `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_relay.py:266-330` - UUID-prefixed relay.
5. `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_agent_relay.py:96-116` - demux to the per-transfer session.
6. `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:71-325` - envelope parse, scope check, response build.
7. `backend/src/yinshi/worker_runtime.py:29` - ASGI dispatch into the worker app.
8. `backend/src/yinshi/api/terminal_channels.py:121-250` - terminal routes.
9. `backend/src/yinshi/api/terminal_channels.py:79-110` - workspace path and sidecar socket resolution, branching on `runtime.socket_path is None`.
10. `backend/src/yinshi/services/terminal_journal.py:85-512` - newline-delimited JSON to the sidecar socket, buffered into sequenced batches (`_append_event:404`, `_split_terminal_data:439`, `_decode_message:512`).
11. `sidecar/src/sidecar.js:1184-1210` - dispatch of `terminal_attach`, `terminal_input`, `terminal_resize`, `terminal_restart`, `terminal_kill`, `terminal_detach`.
12. `sidecar/src/sidecar.js:982-1082` - `pty.spawn`; `onData` emits `terminal_data` at `:999-1003`, `onExit` emits `terminal_exit` at `:1005-1012`, ready emits `terminal_ready` at `:1036-1042`.

### Terminal path B: direct WebSocket proxy

`backend/src/yinshi/api/terminals.py:273-274` exposes `/api/workspaces/{id}/terminal` as a WebSocket with its own sidecar framing helpers: `_send_sidecar:72`, `_read_sidecar:81`, `_proxy_browser_to_sidecar:92`, `_proxy_sidecar_to_browser:169`, `_run_desktop_terminal_proxy:188`. Workspace resolution in `backend/src/yinshi/services/desktop_terminal.py:37`.

Reimplemented logic: sidecar newline-JSON framing exists twice in the backend (`terminals.py:72-91` and `terminal_journal.py:478-512`). Terminal event validation exists in Python (`terminal_journal.py:404-454`) and again in TypeScript (`terminalChannel.ts:47-59`). Size bounds 2 to 500 appear in `terminal_channels.py:37-38,49-51` and `terminalChannel.ts:38-45`.

### Agent stream path A: SSE

1. `frontend/src/hooks/useAgentStream.ts:127-133` calls `streamPrompt`.
2. `frontend/src/api/client.ts:514-570` - POST to `/api/sessions/{id}/prompt`, manual SSE line splitting at `:551-566`, `normalizeEvent` at `:503-512`.
3. `backend/src/yinshi/api/stream.py:771-773` - `prompt_session`; execution context resolved at `:630`.
4. `backend/src/yinshi/services/sidecar.py:39-136` - newline-JSON transport with an 8 MiB message limit.
5. `sidecar/src/sidecar.js:1203-1209` - `query`, `resolve`, `cancel` dispatch; content block shaping at `:244-250`.

### Agent stream path B: polled run journal

1. `frontend/src/hooks/useAgentStream.ts:114-126` calls `startRuntimePrompt`.
2. `frontend/src/runtime/promptStream.ts:30-249` - POST `/runs`, poll `/runs/{id}/events/{seq}`, POST `/cancel`; reuses `normalizeEvent` from `client.ts`.
3. `backend/src/yinshi/api/prompt_runs.py:99-160`.
4. `backend/src/yinshi/services/prompt_journal.py:89-515` - run lifecycle and sequenced batches; `_default_prompt_executor:58` bridges to the same sidecar execution as path A.
5. Same sidecar hops as path A.

Reimplemented logic across the two agent-stream paths: event normalization is shared, but transport, status enums, cancellation, and terminal-status handling are written twice (`client.ts:514-575` versus `promptStream.ts:9-249`). Two journals with near-identical sequenced-batch semantics exist: `prompt_journal.py` and `terminal_journal.py`.

---

## 5. Component dependency map

Frontend:

- `App.tsx` depends on `pages/{Session,Settings,Landing,Login}` and `components/Sidebar`.
- `pages/Session.tsx:19,67` depends on `runtime/useRuntimeResource`, which depends on `runtime/runtimeRef`, `runtime/resolveRuntime`, `runtime/runtimeTransport`.
- `runtime/runtimeTransport.ts` depends on `api/client` (`api`, `hostedApi`), `runner/encryptedRunnerClient`, `runtime/encryptedUpload`.
- `runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts` depends on `crypto/noiseIk` (which depends on noise-c.wasm) and on `api/client` for capability issuance.
- `hooks/useAgentStream.ts` depends on both `api/client.streamPrompt` and `runtime/promptStream`.
- `components/Sidebar.tsx` depends on `runtime/*`, `runner/repositories`, `api/client`.
- `api/client.ts` depends on `window.yinshiDesktop`, typed in `types/desktop.d.ts`.

Desktop:

- `main.ts` depends on `appController`, `helperSupervisor`, `sidecarSupervisor`, `localRuntime`, `runtimeLaunchConfig`, `runtimeSecrets`, `credentialStore`, `diskEncryption`, `hostedApiGateway`, `hostedAccessSession`, `hostedAuth`, `security`, `shellPolicy`, `authCallbackListener`, `localRepositoryImport`, `automaticUpdates`, `desktopApi` (`desktop/src/main.ts:21-48`).
- `preload.ts` depends on `desktopApi` channel names and exposes `window.yinshiDesktop` (`desktop/src/preload.ts:11-30`).
- `helperSupervisor` spawns the backend in `desktop` mode through `backend/src/yinshi/desktop_runtime.py`.
- `sidecarSupervisor` spawns `sidecar/src/index.js` over `SIDECAR_SOCKET_PATH`.

Backend:

- `main.py` depends on `api/*` routers, middleware, `config`, `db`.
- `api/stream.py` and `api/prompt_runs.py` depend on `services/prompt_journal`, which depends on `services/sidecar`.
- `api/terminal_channels.py` depends on `services/terminal_journal`, `services/workspace_runtime_paths`, `services/sidecar_runtime`, `services/container`.
- `api/terminals.py` depends on `services/desktop_terminal` and talks to the sidecar socket directly.
- `api/runners.py` depends on `services/runners`, `services/runner_capabilities`, `services/runner_relay`.
- `runner_agent.py` depends on `services/runner_agent_relay`, which depends on `services/runner_rpc`, `services/runner_noise_session`, `services/runner_noise`; it also depends on `runner_worker.py`, which imports `main.create_app` and `worker_runtime.WorkerHttpDispatcher`.
- `services/control_encryption` depends on `services/crypto`.

Sidecar:

- `index.js` depends on `sidecar.js`, which depends on `git_auth.js`, `git_askpass_client.js`, `constants.js`. No dependency on backend, frontend, or desktop.

### Circular and surprising dependencies

1. Import cycle broken by a deferred import. `backend/src/yinshi/runner_worker.py:264` does `from yinshi.main import create_app` inside a method body, while `main.py` reaches worker code through routers and `worker_auth`. The cycle is real; only the function-local import keeps it working.
2. The backend imports itself across a network boundary. The BYOC runner runs a second full FastAPI app in-process (`runner_worker.py:288`) and calls it over ASGI with no listening socket (`worker_runtime.py`). One codebase is both control plane and remote worker, separated only by `app.state.mode`.
3. Route knowledge is triplicated across three languages (section 3). Highest-risk coupling in the repository.
4. Two terminal subsystems and two agent-stream subsystems coexist, each with its own framing. `api/terminals.py` (WebSocket) and `api/terminal_channels.py` (polling) both talk to the same sidecar through separately written newline-JSON helpers.
5. `api/client.ts` bypasses the runtime abstraction. `DESKTOP_HOSTED_RUNNER_PATHS` at `client.ts:321-325` hard-codes three paths that must use the Electron bridge, independent of `RuntimeRef`. A fourth control-plane path added later would silently take the wrong transport.
6. The default-runtime rule is written three times: `runtimeRef.ts:62-67`, `Sidebar.tsx:172-174`, `Settings.tsx:604-606` and `:697`.
7. Terminology drift: frontend `local`/`hosted`/`byoc`, backend `desktop`/`hosted`/`worker`, deployment terms runner, sidecar, helper. No file records the mapping.
8. The sidecar is the only fully decoupled component. It knows nothing about runtimes, tenants, or Noise, and is a clean extraction boundary.

---

## Start Here

Open `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts` first. Lines 10-17 define the `RuntimeRef` union that drives every frontend branch; lines 46-206 hold the route-to-scope table duplicated in `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:132-215` and `desktop/src/hostedApiGateway.ts:16-170`; lines 259-340 contain the dispatch that selects plain HTTP, the Electron bridge, or the Noise channel. Read `backend/src/yinshi/main.py:379-412` next for the backend mode split.

## Open questions

1. Is the RPC envelope `v: 2` (`encryptedRunnerClient.ts:483`) versus `_REQUEST_KEYS_V1` (`runner_rpc.py:17`) intentional?
2. Does the backend accept the `query` key the frontend always sends? It is absent from `_REQUEST_KEYS_V1`.
3. Is `api/terminals.py` (WebSocket) still live, or superseded by `api/terminal_channels.py` (polling)? Both are registered at `main.py:395-396`.
4. Is `client.ts:streamPrompt` (SSE) still live, or superseded by `promptStream.ts`? `useAgentStream.ts:127` still falls back to it when no runtime transport exists.
