# Yinshi Cross-Cutting Architecture Report

Scope: `backend/src/yinshi` (Python/FastAPI), `frontend/src` (React/Vite), `desktop/src` (Electron/TypeScript), `sidecar/src` (Node). Vendored and build directories excluded.

---

## 1. Noise IK and encryption protocol: no single authoritative definition

There is no shared schema, no IDL, and no generated artifact. The wire protocol is re-derived independently in Python and TypeScript. Matching literal constants are written twice.

### 1a. Noise handshake layer (duplicated constants)

| Constant | Backend | Frontend |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Protocol name `Noise_IK_25519_ChaChaPoly_SHA256` | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise.py:22` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:8` |
| Max message length 65535 | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise.py:26` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:11` |
| IK first message overhead 96 | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise.py:24` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:12` |
| IK second message minimum 48 | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise.py:25` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:13` |
| Rehandshake threshold 1048576 | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise_session.py:24` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:14`, `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:398` |
| X25519 key length 32 | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise.py:23` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:9` |
| Prologue and protocol tag `yinshi-runner-v1` | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise_session.py:23`, `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_capabilities.py:27` | `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:9`, applied at `:411` |

The two implementations use different crypto stacks. Python uses `noiseprotocol` plus `cryptography` at `runner_noise.py:11-20`. The browser uses `@richardhopton/noise-c.wasm` at `noiseIk.ts:1-6`. Parity is maintained only by hand.

### 1b. Capability token layer

Capability tokens are issued and verified only in Python. See `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_capabilities.py:161-306`. Ed25519-signed claims are `scopes`, `token_id`, `transfer_id`, `expires_at`, `max_frame_bytes`, `max_session_bytes`, `initiator_public_key`, and `protocol`. The runner responder consumes them at `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise_session.py:178-225`. It sends the handshake response payload `{"protocol":..., "transfer_id":...}` at `:216-224`. The frontend re-validates the same claim shape independently. See `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:14-25` for the interface and `:118` for `validateCapability`. The handshake reply is parsed at `:449-452`.

### 1c. Relay framing layer (16-byte UUID prefix)

- Hosted relay adds the prefix on client-to-runner traffic at `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_relay.py:266-283` as `uuid.UUID(transfer_id).bytes + ciphertext`.
- Hosted relay strips the prefix on runner-to-client traffic at `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_relay.py:298-330`.
- The runner side parses and re-adds the same prefix at `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_agent_relay.py:96-116`.
- Control messages are hand-built JSON strings, not models. `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_relay.py:262-263` and `:328-330` emit `'{"transfer_id":"..","type":"close"}'`. They are parsed at `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_agent_relay.py:77-95,129-156`.
- The browser never sees the prefix. It sends bare ciphertext and expects the literal readiness string `'{"type":"ready"}'` at `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:441-443`.

### 1d. RPC envelope layer (version mismatch)

- The frontend request envelope sends `v: 2` at `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:472-484`.
- The backend accepted key set is named `_REQUEST_KEYS_V1` and lacks `query`. See `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:17`. Version and type checks are at `:83-100`.
- The response envelope is built at `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:313-325`. It is parsed independently at `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:495-500`.
- Size limits diverge by construction. The browser caps a request at 49152 bytes at `encryptedRunnerClient.ts:487-488`. The responder caps the frame from the capability at `runner_noise_session.py:265-271`. The relay caps at `_RELAY_FRAME_BYTES_MAX` at `runner_relay.py:271`.

Risk: the wire version literal is `2` while the backend constant is named `_REQUEST_KEYS_V1`. Also, `query` appears in the frontend envelope but not in the backend key allowlist.

### 1e. Desktop encryption is a separate, unrelated scheme

`desktop/src/runtimeSecrets.ts:6-11` defines `RuntimeSecrets {version:1, secretKey, encryptionPepper, keyEncryptionKey}`. Those values pass to the Python helper. The backend reads them through settings and derives keys with its own AES-GCM helpers at `backend/src/yinshi/services/crypto.py:48-231` and `backend/src/yinshi/services/control_encryption.py:11-30`. `desktop/src/diskEncryption.ts` only detects FileVault status through `detectFileVaultStatus`, imported at `desktop/src/main.ts:29`. It is not part of the Noise protocol.

### Files requiring coordinated edit for any Noise or wire protocol change

1. `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise.py` (handshake primitives, protocol name, length bounds)
2. `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise_session.py` (prologue, capability binding, handshake reply, frame limits)
3. `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_capabilities.py` (protocol tag, claim schema, scope set)
4. `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py` (RPC envelope, version, route-to-scope table)
5. `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_relay.py` (UUID prefix framing, control JSON, byte limits)
6. `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_agent_relay.py` (runner-side demux, prefix, control JSON)
7. `backend/src/yinshi/api/runner_relay.py` (WebSocket endpoints)
8. `backend/src/yinshi/api/runners.py` (capability issuance, protocol echoed at `:198`)
9. `backend/src/yinshi/runner_agent.py` (relay client, registration, key pinning)
10. `backend/src/yinshi/models.py` (`RunnerCapabilityCreateIn:370`, `RunnerCapabilityOut:393`, `RunnerRegisterIn:324`, `RunnerNoiseKeyConfirmationIn:360`)
11. `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts` (browser handshake, constants)
12. `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts` (prologue, capability validation, RPC envelope, ready string)
13. `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts` (scope selection, session byte budget at `:92`)
14. `frontend/src/runtime/encryptedUpload.ts` (chunked upload over the same channel)
15. `frontend/src/runner/repositories.ts` (BYOC listing path)
16. `frontend/src/types/noise-c-wasm.d.ts` (wasm binding types)
17. Test mirrors: `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.test.ts`, `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.test.ts`, plus backend tests for the five services above.

Desktop is not on this list unless the `desktop/src/hostedApiGateway.ts` route allowlist must change. See section 3.

---

## 2. Type and schema duplication

There is no OpenAPI codegen. `frontend/package.json` has no `openapi` or generate script. The backend serves `/openapi.json` only when `debug` is true, at `backend/src/yinshi/main.py:451`. Every API shape is hand-written twice.

Duplicated pairs. Pydantic models live in `backend/src/yinshi/models.py`. TypeScript interfaces live in `frontend/src/api/client.ts`.

| Shape | Backend | Frontend |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Repo | `models.py:136` `RepoOut` | `client.ts:1` `Repo` |
| Workspace | `models.py:163` `WorkspaceOut` | `client.ts:178` `Workspace` |
| Session | `models.py:212` `SessionOut` | `client.ts:189` `SessionInfo` |
| Message | `models.py:224` `MessageOut` | `client.ts:199` `Message` |
| CloudRunner | `models.py:294` `CloudRunnerOut` | `client.ts:83` `CloudRunner` |
| Runner registration | `models.py:314` `CloudRunnerRegistrationOut` | `client.ts:101` `CloudRunnerRegistration` |
| Runner capability response | `models.py:393` `RunnerCapabilityOut` | `encryptedRunnerClient.ts:14` `RunnerCapabilityResponse` |
| Runner capability request | `models.py:370` `RunnerCapabilityCreateIn` | `encryptedRunnerClient.ts:27` `RunnerCapabilityRequest` |
| Provider descriptor | `models.py:448` | `client.ts:34` |
| Provider setup field | `models.py:439` | `client.ts:27` |
| Model descriptor | `models.py:460` | `client.ts:47` |
| Provider catalog | `models.py:475` | `client.ts:60` |
| Provider auth start | `models.py:483` | `client.ts:109` |
| Provider auth status | `models.py:495` | `client.ts:119` |
| Provider connection | `models.py:602` | `client.ts:66` |
| API key | `models.py:625` | `client.ts:19` |
| Pi config | `models.py:672` | `client.ts:131` |
| Pi command | `models.py:687` | `client.ts:146` |
| Pi config commands | `models.py:702` | `client.ts:153` |
| Pi package release | `models.py:713` | `client.ts:157` |
| Pi release notes | `models.py:724` | `client.ts:166` |
| Prompt request | `models.py:237` `WSPrompt` | inline at `frontend/src/runtime/promptStream.ts:42-49` and `client.ts:514-522` |

Additional duplications outside `models.py`:

- Terminal channel shapes at `backend/src/yinshi/api/terminal_channels.py:36-61` versus hand validators at `frontend/src/runtime/terminalChannel.ts:11-59`. The event-type set is at `:4-9`.
- Prompt run shapes at `backend/src/yinshi/api/prompt_runs.py:99-160` versus `frontend/src/runtime/promptStream.ts:30-40`. The run status enum is duplicated at `promptStream.ts:9-28`.
- SSE event union at `frontend/src/api/client.ts:453-502` mirrors sidecar content shaping at `sidecar/src/sidecar.js:244-250`.
- Desktop IPC contract in `desktop/src/desktopApi.ts` duplicated for the renderer in `frontend/src/types/desktop.d.ts`.
- Runtime secrets contract at `desktop/src/runtimeSecrets.ts:6-11` versus backend settings used by `backend/src/yinshi/config.py` and `services/crypto.py`.

---

## 3. Runtime abstraction: where the runtime decision is made (key finding)

Two orthogonal runtime axes exist. They are not unified.

Axis A is the frontend `RuntimeRef.location` with values `local`, `hosted`, and `byoc`. It is defined at `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:10-17`. The unresolved variant is at `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeRef.ts:6-13`.

Axis B is the backend `AppMode` with values `desktop`, `hosted`, and `worker`. It is selected in `backend/src/yinshi/main.py:415-457` through `create_app(mode=...)`.

The names do not line up. Frontend `local` maps to backend `desktop`. Frontend `byoc` maps to backend `worker` inside `runner_agent`. Frontend `hosted` maps to backend `hosted`. Nothing in the code states or enforces that mapping.

### Decision points, exhaustive

Frontend, 13 sites:

1. `frontend/src/runtime/useRuntimeResource.ts:42-51` is the canonical resolution. It parses the encoded ID, resolves the ref, and builds the transport.
2. `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeRef.ts:62-67`. `defaultRuntimeRef` returns `local` on desktop and `hosted` elsewhere.
3. `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeRef.ts:69-83`. `runtimeResourceId` encodes the runtime into the URL as `hosted.`, `local.`, or `byoc.<b64url>.`.
4. `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeRef.ts:87-119`. `parseRuntimeResourceId` decodes it.
5. `frontend/src/runtime/resolveRuntime.ts:20-45` resolves BYOC by fetching `/api/settings/runner` and requiring `noise_key_confirmed`.
6. `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:259-273` selects `hostedApi` versus `api` when the location is hosted and `window.yinshiDesktop` exists.
7. `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:286-296` dispatches BYOC requests through the encrypted Noise channel.
8. `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:322-340` branches uploads three ways: BYOC encrypted, hosted bridge, plain multipart.
9. `frontend/src/runtime/promptStream.ts:174` sets the poll delay by runtime location.
10. `frontend/src/api/client.ts:321-325, 374-378, 402-410` routes to the bridge using the hard-coded `DESKTOP_HOSTED_RUNNER_PATHS` set. This bypasses `RuntimeRef`.
11. `frontend/src/api/piCommandsCache.ts:22` namespaces the cache key by runtime.

### Circular and surprising dependencies

1. An import cycle is broken by a deferred import. `backend/src/yinshi/runner_worker.py:264` imports `create_app` from `yinshi.main` inside a method body. `main.py` reaches worker code through routers and `worker_auth`. Only the function-local import keeps this working.
2. The backend imports itself across a network boundary. The BYOC runner runs a second full FastAPI app in-process at `runner_worker.py:288`. It calls that app over ASGI with no listening socket, in `worker_runtime.py`. One codebase is both control plane and remote worker, separated only by `app.state.mode`.
3. Route knowledge is triplicated across three languages. See section 3. This is the highest-risk coupling in the repository.
4. Two terminal subsystems and two agent-stream subsystems coexist, each with its own framing. `api/terminals.py` and `api/terminal_channels.py` both talk to the same sidecar through separately written newline-JSON helpers.
5. `api/client.ts` bypasses the runtime abstraction. `DESKTOP_HOSTED_RUNNER_PATHS` at `client.ts:321-325` hard-codes three paths that must use the Electron bridge. A fourth control-plane path added later would silently take the wrong transport.
6. The default-runtime rule is written three times: `runtimeRef.ts:62-67`, `Sidebar.tsx:172-174`, and `Settings.tsx:604-606` plus `:697`.
7. Terminology drifts across layers. The frontend says `local`, `hosted`, `byoc`. The backend says `desktop`, `hosted`, `worker`. Deployment docs say runner, sidecar, helper. No file records the mapping.
8. The sidecar is the only fully decoupled component. It knows nothing about runtimes, tenants, or Noise. It is a clean extraction boundary.

## 1. Noise IK and encryption protocol: no single authoritative definition

There is no shared schema, no IDL, and no generated artifact. The wire protocol is re-derived independently in Python and TypeScript. Matching literal constants are written twice.

### 1a. Noise handshake layer (duplicated constants)

| Constant | Backend | Frontend |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Protocol name `Noise_IK_25519_ChaChaPoly_SHA256` | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise.py:22` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:8` |
| Max message length 65535 | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise.py:26` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:11` |
| IK first message overhead 96 | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise.py:24` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:12` |
| IK second message minimum 48 | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise.py:25` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:13` |
| Rehandshake threshold 1048576 | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise_session.py:24` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:14`, `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:398` |
| X25519 key length 32 | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise.py:23` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:9` |
| Prologue and protocol tag `yinshi-runner-v1` | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise_session.py:23`, `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_capabilities.py:27` | `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:9`, applied at `:411` |

The two implementations use different crypto stacks. Python uses `noiseprotocol` plus `cryptography` at `runner_noise.py:11-20`. The browser uses `@richardhopton/noise-c.wasm` at `noiseIk.ts:1-6`. Parity is maintained only by hand.

### 1b. Capability token layer

Capability tokens are issued and verified only in Python. See `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_capabilities.py:161-306`. Ed25519-signed claims are `scopes`, `token_id`, `transfer_id`, `expires_at`, `max_frame_bytes`, `max_session_bytes`, `initiator_public_key`, and `protocol`. The runner responder consumes them at `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise_session.py:178-225`. It sends the handshake response payload `{"protocol":..., "transfer_id":...}` at `:216-224`. The frontend re-validates the same claim shape independently. See `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:14-25` for the interface and `:118` for `validateCapability`. The handshake reply is parsed at `:449-452`.

### 1c. Relay framing layer (16-byte UUID prefix)

- Hosted relay adds the prefix on client-to-runner traffic at `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_relay.py:266-283` as `uuid.UUID(transfer_id).bytes + ciphertext`.
- Hosted relay strips the prefix on runner-to-client traffic at `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_relay.py:298-330`.
- The runner side parses and re-adds the same prefix at `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_agent_relay.py:96-116`.
- Control messages are hand-built JSON strings, not models. `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_relay.py:262-263` and `:328-330` emit `'{"transfer_id":"..","type":"close"}'`. They are parsed at `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_agent_relay.py:77-95,129-156`.
- The browser never sees the prefix. It sends bare ciphertext and expects the literal readiness string `'{"type":"ready"}'` at `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:441-443`.

### 1d. RPC envelope layer (version mismatch)

- The frontend request envelope sends `v: 2` at `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:472-484`.
- The backend accepted key set is named `_REQUEST_KEYS_V1` and lacks `query`. See `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:17`. Version and type checks are at `:83-100`.
- The response envelope is built at `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:313-325`. It is parsed independently at `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:495-500`.
- Size limits diverge by construction. The browser caps a request at 49152 bytes at `encryptedRunnerClient.ts:487-488`. The responder caps the frame from the capability at `runner_noise_session.py:265-271`. The relay caps at `_RELAY_FRAME_BYTES_MAX` at `runner_relay.py:271`.

Risk: the wire version literal is `2` while the backend constant is named `_REQUEST_KEYS_V1`. Also, `query` appears in the frontend envelope but not in the backend key allowlist.

### 1e. Desktop encryption is a separate, unrelated scheme

`desktop/src/runtimeSecrets.ts:6-11` defines `RuntimeSecrets {version:1, secretKey, encryptionPepper, keyEncryptionKey}`. Those values pass to the Python helper. The backend reads them through settings and derives keys with its own AES-GCM helpers at `backend/src/yinshi/services/crypto.py:48-231` and `backend/src/yinshi/services/control_encryption.py:11-30`. `desktop/src/diskEncryption.ts` only detects FileVault status through `detectFileVaultStatus`, imported at `desktop/src/main.ts:29`. It is not part of the Noise protocol.

## 3. Runtime abstraction: where the runtime decision is made (key finding)

Two orthogonal runtime axes exist. They are not unified.

Axis A is the frontend `RuntimeRef.location` with values `local`, `hosted`, and `byoc`. It is defined at `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:10-17`. The unresolved variant is at `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeRef.ts:6-13`.

Axis B is the backend `AppMode` with values `desktop`, `hosted`, and `worker`. It is selected in `backend/src/yinshi/main.py:415-457` through `create_app(mode=...)`.

The names do not line up. Frontend `local` maps to backend `desktop`. Frontend `byoc` maps to backend `worker` inside `runner_agent`. Frontend `hosted` maps to backend `hosted`. Nothing in the code states or enforces that mapping.

1. `frontend/src/runtime/useRuntimeResource.ts:42-51` is the canonical resolution. It parses the encoded ID, resolves the ref, and builds the transport.
2. `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeRef.ts:62-67`. `defaultRuntimeRef` returns `local` on desktop and `hosted` elsewhere.
3. `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeRef.ts:69-83`. `runtimeResourceId` encodes the runtime into the URL as `hosted.`, `local.`, or `byoc.<b64url>.`.
4. `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeRef.ts:87-119`. `parseRuntimeResourceId` decodes it.
5. `frontend/src/runtime/resolveRuntime.ts:20-45` resolves BYOC by fetching `/api/settings/runner` and requiring `noise_key_confirmed`.
6. `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:259-273` selects `hostedApi` versus `api` when the location is hosted and `window.yinshiDesktop` exists.
7. `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:286-296` dispatches BYOC requests through the encrypted Noise channel.
8. `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:322-340` branches uploads three ways: BYOC encrypted, hosted bridge, plain multipart.
9. `frontend/src/runtime/promptStream.ts:174` sets the poll delay by runtime location.
10. `frontend/src/api/client.ts:321-325, 374-378, 402-410` routes to the bridge using the hard-coded `DESKTOP_HOSTED_RUNNER_PATHS` set. This bypasses `RuntimeRef`.
11. `frontend/src/api/piCommandsCache.ts:22` namespaces the cache key by runtime.
12. `frontend/src/components/Sidebar.tsx:172-247, 269, 514, 973, 1096, 1132, 1161` discovers and aggregates all three locations. It rebuilds the default runtime at `:172-174` instead of calling `defaultRuntimeRef`.
13. `frontend/src/pages/Settings.tsx:604-606, 631-638, 697, 716, 757-764` holds a third open-coded copy of the default-runtime rule at `:604-606` and `:697`.

Backend mode branches:

14. `backend/src/yinshi/main.py:415-424`. `create_app` validates the mode.
15. `backend/src/yinshi/main.py:309-322`. Worker mode uses a distinct middleware stack and returns early.
16. `backend/src/yinshi/main.py:344-352`. Desktop mode injects `DesktopTenantMiddleware` with the fixed `desktop-local` tenant.
17. `backend/src/yinshi/main.py:361-363`. Desktop mode uses a different content security policy.
18. `backend/src/yinshi/main.py:379-412`. `_include_routes` splits execution routers from control routers. Only `hosted` receives auth, runners, relay, GitHub, and desktop devices.
19. `backend/src/yinshi/main.py:266`. Hosted-only startup work.
20. `backend/src/yinshi/runner_worker.py:264-293`. The runner agent builds `create_app(mode="worker", ...)` in-process.
21. `backend/src/yinshi/worker_runtime.py:29-40`. `WorkerHttpDispatcher` asserts `app.state.mode == "worker"` and dispatches over ASGI with no socket.
22. `backend/src/yinshi/api/terminal_channels.py:97-105`. Execution-time branch. With no sidecar socket path it uses the settings socket and host workspace path. Otherwise it remaps the path into the container.
23. `backend/src/yinshi/services/sidecar_runtime.py:30-38`. `TenantSidecarContext` with a nullable `socket_path` is the mechanism behind that branch.
24. `backend/src/yinshi/api/terminals.py:188-274`. A separate desktop terminal WebSocket proxy, parallel to the polling channel API.
25. `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:132-215`. Route-to-scope table gating what a BYOC runtime may execute.

Desktop:

26. `desktop/src/main.ts:369` and `desktop/src/runtimeLaunchConfig.ts:120-160` set helper and sidecar socket paths and environment for the local runtime.
27. `desktop/src/localRuntime.ts:15-30` asserts helper and sidecar agree on `SIDECAR_SOCKET_PATH`, then starts the pair.
28. `desktop/src/hostedApiGateway.ts:16-170` allowlists hosted API routes reachable through the bridge. This is the third copy of the route table.
29. `desktop/src/helperSupervisor.ts` and `desktop/src/sidecarSupervisor.ts`, imported at `desktop/src/main.ts:32,48`, own local runtime process lifecycle.

Sidecar:

30. `sidecar/src/sidecar.js:937` reads the socket path from `SIDECAR_SOCKET_PATH`.
31. `sidecar/src/sidecar.js:946` toggles dotenv on `SIDECAR_LOAD_DOTENV === "1"`. Desktop sets `"0"` at `desktop/src/runtimeLaunchConfig.ts:158`.
32. `sidecar/src/sidecar.js:1154-1210` holds one message-type dispatch table. The sidecar is runtime-agnostic.

### Triplicated route-to-scope and allowlist table

The same URL surface is enumerated three times, in three languages, for three purposes.

- `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:132-215` performs authoritative server-side scope enforcement.
- `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:46-206` performs client-side scope selection for capability requests.
- `desktop/src/hostedApiGateway.ts:16-170` performs Electron bridge allowlisting.

Any new API route requires edits in all three files plus the FastAPI router. Divergence here is a security-relevant defect class.

---

## 4. Terminal and agent-stream data paths

### Terminal path A: polling channel, required for BYOC

1. `frontend/src/runtime/terminalChannel.ts:82`. `openRuntimeTerminal` posts to `/api/workspaces/{id}/terminals` and polls `/events/{sequence}`. Event validation is at `:4-9,47-59`.
2. `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:286-296` wraps each BYOC call in a Noise RPC.
3. `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:441-520` performs the handshake and the encrypted request.
4. `backend/src/yinshi/api/runner_relay.py` and `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_relay.py:266-330` perform UUID-prefixed relaying.
5. `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_agent_relay.py:96-116` demuxes to the per-transfer session.
6. `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:71-325` parses the envelope, checks scope, and builds the response.
7. `backend/src/yinshi/worker_runtime.py:29` dispatches into the worker app over ASGI.
8. `backend/src/yinshi/api/terminal_channels.py:121-250` holds the terminal routes.
9. `backend/src/yinshi/api/terminal_channels.py:79-110` resolves workspace paths and the sidecar socket.
10. `backend/src/yinshi/services/terminal_journal.py:85-512` writes newline-delimited JSON to the sidecar socket. Output is buffered into sequenced batches at `_append_event:404`, `_split_terminal_data:439`, and `_decode_message:512`.
11. `sidecar/src/sidecar.js:1184-1210` dispatches `terminal_attach`, `terminal_input`, `terminal_resize`, `terminal_restart`, `terminal_kill`, and `terminal_detach`.
12. `sidecar/src/sidecar.js:982-1082` spawns the pty. `onData` emits `terminal_data` at `:999-1003`. `onExit` emits `terminal_exit` at `:1005-1012`. Ready emits `terminal_ready` at `:1036-1042`.

### Terminal path B: direct WebSocket proxy

`backend/src/yinshi/api/terminals.py:273-274` exposes `/api/workspaces/{id}/terminal` as a WebSocket. It has its own sidecar framing helpers at `_send_sidecar:72`, `_read_sidecar:81`, `_proxy_browser_to_sidecar:92`, `_proxy_sidecar_to_browser:169`, and `_run_desktop_terminal_proxy:188`. Workspace resolution is at `backend/src/yinshi/services/desktop_terminal.py:37`.

Reimplemented logic: sidecar newline-JSON framing exists twice in the backend, at `terminals.py:72-91` and `terminal_journal.py:478-512`. Terminal event validation exists in Python at `terminal_journal.py:404-454` and again in TypeScript at `terminalChannel.ts:47-59`. Size bounds 2 to 500 appear at `terminal_channels.py:37-38,49-51` and `terminalChannel.ts:38-45`.

### Agent stream path A: SSE

1. `frontend/src/hooks/useAgentStream.ts:127-133` calls `streamPrompt`.
2. `frontend/src/api/client.ts:514-570` posts to `/api/sessions/{id}/prompt`. Manual SSE line splitting is at `:551-566`. `normalizeEvent` is at `:503-512`.
3. `backend/src/yinshi/api/stream.py:771-773` handles `prompt_session`. Execution context is resolved at `:630`.
4. `backend/src/yinshi/services/sidecar.py:39-136` provides newline-JSON transport with an 8 MiB message limit.
5. `sidecar/src/sidecar.js:1203-1209` dispatches `query`, `resolve`, and `cancel`. Content block shaping is at `:244-250`.

### Agent stream path B: polled run journal

1. `frontend/src/hooks/useAgentStream.ts:114-126` calls `startRuntimePrompt`.
2. `frontend/src/runtime/promptStream.ts:30-249` posts `/runs`, polls `/runs/{id}/events/{seq}`, and posts `/cancel`. It reuses `normalizeEvent` from `client.ts`.
3. `backend/src/yinshi/api/prompt_runs.py:99-160` holds the routes.
4. `backend/src/yinshi/services/prompt_journal.py:89-515` owns run lifecycle and sequenced batches. `_default_prompt_executor:58` bridges to the same sidecar execution as path A.
5. The remaining sidecar hops match path A.

Reimplemented logic across the two agent-stream paths: event normalization is shared, but transport, status enums, cancellation, and terminal-status handling are written twice. Compare `client.ts:514-575` with `promptStream.ts:9-249`. Two journals with near-identical sequenced-batch semantics exist: `prompt_journal.py` and `terminal_journal.py`.

---

## 5. Component dependency map

Frontend:

- `App.tsx` depends on `pages/{Session,Settings,Landing,Login}` and `components/Sidebar`.
- `pages/Session.tsx:19,67` depends on `runtime/useRuntimeResource`. That depends on `runtime/runtimeRef`, `runtime/resolveRuntime`, and `runtime/runtimeTransport`.
- `runtime/runtimeTransport.ts` depends on `api/client`, `runner/encryptedRunnerClient`, and `runtime/encryptedUpload`.
- `runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts` depends on `crypto/noiseIk`, which depends on noise-c.wasm. It also depends on `api/client` for capability issuance.
- `hooks/useAgentStream.ts` depends on both `api/client.streamPrompt` and `runtime/promptStream`.
- `components/Sidebar.tsx` depends on `runtime/*`, `runner/repositories`, and `api/client`.
- `api/client.ts` depends on `window.yinshiDesktop`, typed in `types/desktop.d.ts`.

Desktop:

- `main.ts` depends on `appController`, `helperSupervisor`, `sidecarSupervisor`, `localRuntime`, `runtimeLaunchConfig`, `runtimeSecrets`, `credentialStore`, `diskEncryption`, `hostedApiGateway`, `hostedAccessSession`, `hostedAuth`, `security`, `shellPolicy`, `authCallbackListener`, `localRepositoryImport`, `automaticUpdates`, and `desktopApi`. See `desktop/src/main.ts:21-48`.
- `preload.ts` depends on `desktopApi` channel names and exposes `window.yinshiDesktop` at `desktop/src/preload.ts:11-30`.
- `helperSupervisor` spawns the backend in desktop mode through `backend/src/yinshi/desktop_runtime.py`.
- `sidecarSupervisor` spawns `sidecar/src/index.js` over `SIDECAR_SOCKET_PATH`.

Backend:

- `main.py` depends on `api/*` routers, middleware, `config`, and `db`.
- `api/stream.py` and `api/prompt_runs.py` depend on `services/prompt_journal`, which depends on `services/sidecar`.
- `api/terminal_channels.py` depends on `services/terminal_journal`, `services/workspace_runtime_paths`, `services/sidecar_runtime`, and `services/container`.
- `api/terminals.py` depends on `services/desktop_terminal` and talks to the sidecar socket directly.
- `api/runners.py` depends on `services/runners`, `services/runner_capabilities`, and `services/runner_relay`.
- `runner_agent.py` depends on `services/runner_agent_relay`. That depends on `services/runner_rpc`, `services/runner_noise_session`, and `services/runner_noise`. `runner_agent.py` also depends on `runner_worker.py`, which imports `main.create_app` and `worker_runtime.WorkerHttpDispatcher`.
- `services/control_encryption` depends on `services/crypto`.

Sidecar:

- `index.js` depends on `sidecar.js`. That depends on `git_auth.js`, `git_askpass_client.js`, and `constants.js`. There is no dependency on backend, frontend, or desktop.

### Circular and surprising dependencies

1. An import cycle is broken by a deferred import. `backend/src/yinshi/runner_worker.py:264` imports `create_app` from `yinshi.main` inside a method body. `main.py` reaches worker code through routers and `worker_auth`. Only the function-local import keeps this working.
2. The backend imports itself across a network boundary. The BYOC runner runs a second full FastAPI app in-process at `runner_worker.py:288`. It calls that app over ASGI with no listening socket, in `worker_runtime.py`. One codebase is both control plane and remote worker, separated only by `app.state.mode`.
3. Route knowledge is triplicated across three languages. See section 3. This is the highest-risk coupling in the repository.
4. Two terminal subsystems and two agent-stream subsystems coexist, each with its own framing. `api/terminals.py` and `api/terminal_channels.py` both talk to the same sidecar through separately written newline-JSON helpers.
5. `api/client.ts` bypasses the runtime abstraction. `DESKTOP_HOSTED_RUNNER_PATHS` at `client.ts:321-325` hard-codes three paths that must use the Electron bridge. A fourth control-plane path added later would silently take the wrong transport.
6. The default-runtime rule is written three times: `runtimeRef.ts:62-67`, `Sidebar.tsx:172-174`, and `Settings.tsx:604-606` plus `:697`.
7. Terminology drifts across layers. The frontend says `local`, `hosted`, `byoc`. The backend says `desktop`, `hosted`, `worker`. Deployment docs say runner, sidecar, helper. No file records the mapping.
8. The sidecar is the only fully decoupled component. It knows nothing about runtimes, tenants, or Noise. It is a clean extraction boundary.

---

## Start Here

Open `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts` first. Lines 10-17 define the `RuntimeRef` union that drives every frontend branch. Lines 46-206 hold the route-to-scope table duplicated in `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:132-215` and `desktop/src/hostedApiGateway.ts:16-170`. Lines 259-340 contain the dispatch that selects plain HTTP, the Electron bridge, or the Noise channel. Read `backend/src/yinshi/main.py:379-412` next for the backend mode split.

## Open questions

1. Is the RPC envelope `v: 2` at `encryptedRunnerClient.ts:483` intentional against `_REQUEST_KEYS_V1` at `runner_rpc.py:17`?
2. Does the backend accept the `query` key the frontend always sends? It is absent from `_REQUEST_KEYS_V1`.
3. Is `api/terminals.py` still live, or superseded by `api/terminal_channels.py`? Both are registered at `main.py:395-396`.
4. Is `client.ts:streamPrompt` still live, or superseded by `promptStream.ts`? `useAgentStream.ts:127` still falls back to it without a runtime transport.
"
}

# Yinshi Cross-Cutting Architecture Report

Scope is `backend/src/yinshi` (Python, FastAPI), `frontend/src` (React, Vite), `desktop/src` (Electron, TypeScript), and `sidecar/src` (Node). Vendored and build directories were excluded.

## 1. Noise IK and encryption protocol

There is no single authoritative definition. No shared schema, no IDL, and no generated artifact exist. The wire protocol is re-derived independently in Python and TypeScript, and matching literal constants are written twice.

The handshake layer duplicates every constant across the language boundary.

| Constant | Backend | Frontend |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Protocol name `Noise_IK_25519_ChaChaPoly_SHA256` | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise.py:22` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:8` |
| Max message length 65535 | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise.py:26` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:11` |
| IK first message overhead 96 | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise.py:24` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:12` |
| IK second message minimum 48 | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise.py:25` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:13` |
| Rehandshake threshold 1048576 | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise_session.py:24` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:14`, `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:398` |
| X25519 key length 32 | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise.py:23` | `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.ts:9` |
| Prologue and protocol tag `yinshi-runner-v1` | `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise_session.py:23`, `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_capabilities.py:27` | `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:9`, applied at `:411` |

The two sides also use different crypto stacks. Python uses `noiseprotocol` plus `cryptography` at `runner_noise.py:11-20`. The browser uses `@richardhopton/noise-c.wasm` at `noiseIk.ts:1-6`. Parity is maintained only by hand.

Capability tokens are issued and verified only in Python, at `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_capabilities.py:161-306`. The Ed25519-signed claims are `scopes`, `token_id`, `transfer_id`, `expires_at`, `max_frame_bytes`, `max_session_bytes`, `initiator_public_key`, and `protocol`. The runner responder consumes them at `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise_session.py:178-225` and sends the handshake response payload `{"protocol":..., "transfer_id":...}` at `:216-224`. The frontend re-validates the same claim shape independently through the `RunnerCapabilityResponse` interface at `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:14-25` and `validateCapability` at `:118`, then parses the handshake reply at `:449-452`.

The relay framing layer adds a 16-byte UUID prefix that only the two Python endpoints understand. The hosted relay adds the prefix on client-to-runner traffic at `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_relay.py:266-283` as `uuid.UUID(transfer_id).bytes + ciphertext`, and strips it on runner-to-client traffic at `:298-330`. The runner side parses and re-adds the same prefix at `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_agent_relay.py:96-116`. Control messages are hand-built JSON strings rather than models. `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_relay.py:262-263` and `:328-330` emit `'{"transfer_id":"..","type":"close"}'`, parsed at `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_agent_relay.py:77-95,129-156`. The browser never sees the prefix. It sends bare ciphertext and expects the literal readiness string `'{"type":"ready"}'` at `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:441-443`.

The RPC envelope layer carries a version mismatch. The frontend request envelope sends `v: 2` at `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:472-484`, while the backend accepted key set is named `_REQUEST_KEYS_V1` at `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:17` and lacks `query`. Version and type checks run at `:83-100`. The response envelope is built at `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:313-325` and parsed independently at `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:495-500`. Size limits diverge by construction. The browser caps a request at 49152 bytes at `encryptedRunnerClient.ts:487-488`, the responder caps the frame from the capability at `runner_noise_session.py:265-271`, and the relay caps at `_RELAY_FRAME_BYTES_MAX` at `runner_relay.py:271`. Both the version-name mismatch and the missing `query` key are open risks.

Desktop encryption is a separate, unrelated scheme. `desktop/src/runtimeSecrets.ts:6-11` defines `RuntimeSecrets {version:1, secretKey, encryptionPepper, keyEncryptionKey}` and passes those values to the Python helper. The backend reads them through settings and derives keys with its own AES-GCM helpers at `backend/src/yinshi/services/crypto.py:48-231` and `backend/src/yinshi/services/control_encryption.py:11-30`. `desktop/src/diskEncryption.ts` only detects FileVault status through `detectFileVaultStatus`, imported at `desktop/src/main.ts:29`, and takes no part in the Noise protocol.

A protocol change requires coordinated edits in seventeen places. On the backend those are `services/runner_noise.py` for handshake primitives and length bounds, `services/runner_noise_session.py` for the prologue, capability binding, handshake reply, and frame limits, `services/runner_capabilities.py` for the protocol tag, claim schema, and scope set, `services/runner_rpc.py` for the envelope, version, and route-to-scope table, `services/runner_relay.py` for prefix framing, control JSON, and byte limits, `services/runner_agent_relay.py` for runner-side demux, `api/runner_relay.py` for the WebSocket endpoints, `api/runners.py` for capability issuance with the protocol echoed at `:198`, `runner_agent.py` for the relay client, registration, and key pinning, and `models.py` for `RunnerCapabilityCreateIn:370`, `RunnerCapabilityOut:393`, `RunnerRegisterIn:324`, and `RunnerNoiseKeyConfirmationIn:360`. On the frontend those are `crypto/noiseIk.ts`, `runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts`, `runtime/runtimeTransport.ts` for scope selection and the session byte budget at `:92`, `runtime/encryptedUpload.ts`, `runner/repositories.ts`, and `types/noise-c-wasm.d.ts`. Test mirrors in `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.test.ts`, `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.test.ts`, and the backend suites for those five services also change. Desktop is affected only when the `desktop/src/hostedApiGateway.ts` route allowlist must change, covered in section 3.

## 2. Type and schema duplication

There is no OpenAPI codegen. `frontend/package.json` has no `openapi` or generate script, and the backend serves `/openapi.json` only when `debug` is true, at `backend/src/yinshi/main.py:451`. Every API shape is hand-written twice, with Pydantic models in `backend/src/yinshi/models.py` and TypeScript interfaces in `frontend/src/api/client.ts`.

| Shape | Backend | Frontend |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Repo | `models.py:136` `RepoOut` | `client.ts:1` `Repo` |
| Workspace | `models.py:163` `WorkspaceOut` | `client.ts:178` `Workspace` |
| Session | `models.py:212` `SessionOut` | `client.ts:189` `SessionInfo` |
| Message | `models.py:224` `MessageOut` | `client.ts:199` `Message` |
| CloudRunner | `models.py:294` `CloudRunnerOut` | `client.ts:83` `CloudRunner` |
| Runner registration | `models.py:314` `CloudRunnerRegistrationOut` | `client.ts:101` `CloudRunnerRegistration` |
| Runner capability response | `models.py:393` `RunnerCapabilityOut` | `encryptedRunnerClient.ts:14` `RunnerCapabilityResponse` |
| Runner capability request | `models.py:370` `RunnerCapabilityCreateIn` | `encryptedRunnerClient.ts:27` `RunnerCapabilityRequest` |
| Provider descriptor | `models.py:448` | `client.ts:34` |
| Provider setup field | `models.py:439` | `client.ts:27` |
| Model descriptor | `models.py:460` | `client.ts:47` |
| Provider catalog | `models.py:475` | `client.ts:60` |
| Provider auth start | `models.py:483` | `client.ts:109` |
| Provider auth status | `models.py:495` | `client.ts:119` |
| Provider connection | `models.py:602` | `client.ts:66` |
| API key | `models.py:625` | `client.ts:19` |
| Pi config | `models.py:672` | `client.ts:131` |
| Pi command | `models.py:687` | `client.ts:146` |
| Pi config commands | `models.py:702` | `client.ts:153` |
| Pi package release | `models.py:713` | `client.ts:157` |
| Pi release notes | `models.py:724` | `client.ts:166` |
| Prompt request | `models.py:237` `WSPrompt` | inline at `frontend/src/runtime/promptStream.ts:42-49` and `client.ts:514-522` |

Four more duplications sit outside `models.py`. Terminal channel shapes appear at `backend/src/yinshi/api/terminal_channels.py:36-61` and again as hand validators at `frontend/src/runtime/terminalChannel.ts:11-59`, with the event-type set at `:4-9`. Prompt run shapes appear at `backend/src/yinshi/api/prompt_runs.py:99-160` and at `frontend/src/runtime/promptStream.ts:30-40`, with the run status enum duplicated at `promptStream.ts:9-28`. The SSE event union at `frontend/src/api/client.ts:453-502` mirrors sidecar content shaping at `sidecar/src/sidecar.js:244-250`. The desktop IPC contract in `desktop/src/desktopApi.ts` is duplicated for the renderer in `frontend/src/types/desktop.d.ts`, and the runtime secrets contract at `desktop/src/runtimeSecrets.ts:6-11` is mirrored by backend settings used in `backend/src/yinshi/config.py` and `services/crypto.py`.

## 3. Runtime abstraction and where the runtime decision is made

This is the key finding. Two orthogonal runtime axes exist, and they are not unified.

Axis A is the frontend `RuntimeRef.location`, with values `local`, `hosted`, and `byoc`. It is defined at `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:10-17`, and the unresolved variant sits at `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeRef.ts:6-13`. Axis B is the backend `AppMode`, with values `desktop`, `hosted`, and `worker`, selected in `backend/src/yinshi/main.py:415-457` through `create_app(mode=...)`. The names do not line up. Frontend `local` maps to backend `desktop`, frontend `byoc` maps to backend `worker` running inside `runner_agent`, and frontend `hosted` maps to backend `hosted`. Nothing in the code states or enforces that mapping.

The frontend branches on runtime in thirteen places. `frontend/src/runtime/useRuntimeResource.ts:42-51` is the canonical resolution, parsing the encoded ID, resolving the ref, and building the transport. In `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeRef.ts`, `defaultRuntimeRef` at `:62-67` returns `local` on desktop and `hosted` elsewhere, `runtimeResourceId` at `:69-83` encodes the runtime into the URL as `hosted.`, `local.`, or `byoc.<b64url>.`, and `parseRuntimeResourceId` at `:87-119` decodes it. `frontend/src/runtime/resolveRuntime.ts:20-45` resolves BYOC by fetching `/api/settings/runner` and requiring `noise_key_confirmed`. Inside `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts`, line range `259-273` selects `hostedApi` against `api` when the location is hosted and `window.yinshiDesktop` exists, `286-296` dispatches BYOC requests through the encrypted Noise channel, and `322-340` branches uploads three ways across BYOC encryption, the hosted bridge, and plain multipart. `frontend/src/runtime/promptStream.ts:174` sets the poll delay by runtime location. `frontend/src/api/client.ts:321-325, 374-378, 402-410` routes to the bridge using the hard-coded `DESKTOP_HOSTED_RUNNER_PATHS` set, which bypasses `RuntimeRef` entirely. `frontend/src/api/piCommandsCache.ts:22` namespaces the cache key by runtime. `frontend/src/components/Sidebar.tsx:172-247, 269, 514, 973, 1096, 1132, 1161` discovers and aggregates all three locations, and rebuilds the default runtime at `:172-174` instead of calling `defaultRuntimeRef`. `frontend/src/pages/Settings.tsx:604-606, 631-638, 697, 716, 757-764` holds a third open-coded copy of that same default-runtime rule at `:604-606` and `:697`.

The backend branches on mode in twelve places. `backend/src/yinshi/main.py:415-424` validates the mode inside `create_app`. Worker mode uses a distinct middleware stack and returns early at `:309-322`. Desktop mode injects `DesktopTenantMiddleware` with the fixed `desktop-local` tenant at `:344-352` and uses a different content security policy at `:361-363`. `_include_routes` at `:379-412` splits execution routers from control routers, so only hosted mode receives auth, runners, the relay, GitHub, and desktop devices. Hosted-only startup work runs at `:266`. The runner agent builds `create_app(mode="worker", ...)` in-process at `backend/src/yinshi/runner_worker.py:264-293`, and `WorkerHttpDispatcher` at `backend/src/yinshi/worker_runtime.py:29-40` asserts `app.state.mode == "worker"` before dispatching over ASGI with no socket. An execution-time branch at `backend/src/yinshi/api/terminal_channels.py:97-105` uses the settings socket and the host workspace path when no sidecar socket path exists, and otherwise remaps the path into the container. The mechanism behind that branch is `TenantSidecarContext` with a nullable `socket_path` at `backend/src/yinshi/services/sidecar_runtime.py:30-38`. A separate desktop terminal WebSocket proxy runs in parallel to the polling channel API at `backend/src/yinshi/api/terminals.py:188-274`. The route-to-scope table at `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:132-215` gates what a BYOC runtime may execute.

Desktop branches in four places. `desktop/src/main.ts:369` and `desktop/src/runtimeLaunchConfig.ts:120-160` set helper and sidecar socket paths and environment for the local runtime. `desktop/src/localRuntime.ts:15-30` asserts that helper and sidecar agree on `SIDECAR_SOCKET_PATH` before starting the pair. `desktop/src/hostedApiGateway.ts:16-170` allowlists the hosted API routes reachable through the bridge, which is the third copy of the route table. `desktop/src/helperSupervisor.ts` and `desktop/src/sidecarSupervisor.ts`, imported at `desktop/src/main.ts:32,48`, own local runtime process lifecycle.

The sidecar branches in three places, none of which concern runtime kind. `sidecar/src/sidecar.js:937` reads the socket path from `SIDECAR_SOCKET_PATH`, `:946` toggles dotenv on `SIDECAR_LOAD_DOTENV === "1"` while desktop sets `"0"` at `desktop/src/runtimeLaunchConfig.ts:158`, and `:1154-1210` holds one message-type dispatch table. The sidecar is runtime-agnostic.

The same URL surface is enumerated three times, in three languages, for three purposes. `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:132-215` performs authoritative server-side scope enforcement. `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:46-206` performs client-side scope selection for capability requests. `desktop/src/hostedApiGateway.ts:16-170` performs Electron bridge allowlisting. Any new API route requires edits in all three files plus the FastAPI router, and divergence here is a security-relevant defect class.

## 4. Terminal and agent-stream data paths

The polling terminal channel is the path required for BYOC, and it crosses twelve hops. `frontend/src/runtime/terminalChannel.ts:82` posts to `/api/workspaces/{id}/terminals` and polls `/events/{sequence}`, validating events at `:4-9,47-59`. `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:286-296` wraps each BYOC call in a Noise RPC, and `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:441-520` performs the handshake and encrypted request. `backend/src/yinshi/api/runner_relay.py` with `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_relay.py:266-330` relays UUID-prefixed frames, and `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_agent_relay.py:96-116` demuxes to the per-transfer session. `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:71-325` parses the envelope, checks scope, and builds the response, then `backend/src/yinshi/worker_runtime.py:29` dispatches into the worker app over ASGI. `backend/src/yinshi/api/terminal_channels.py:121-250` holds the terminal routes and `:79-110` resolves workspace paths and the sidecar socket. `backend/src/yinshi/services/terminal_journal.py:85-512` writes newline-delimited JSON to the sidecar socket and buffers output into sequenced batches at `_append_event:404`, `_split_terminal_data:439`, and `_decode_message:512`. Finally `sidecar/src/sidecar.js:1184-1210` dispatches the terminal message types, and `:982-1082` spawns the pty, with `onData` emitting `terminal_data` at `:999-1003`, `onExit` emitting `terminal_exit` at `:1005-1012`, and ready emitting `terminal_ready` at `:1036-1042`.

A second terminal path exists as a direct WebSocket proxy. `backend/src/yinshi/api/terminals.py:273-274` exposes `/api/workspaces/{id}/terminal` with its own sidecar framing helpers at `_send_sidecar:72`, `_read_sidecar:81`, `_proxy_browser_to_sidecar:92`, `_proxy_sidecar_to_browser:169`, and `_run_desktop_terminal_proxy:188`. Workspace resolution runs at `backend/src/yinshi/services/desktop_terminal.py:37`. Sidecar newline-JSON framing therefore exists twice inside the backend, at `terminals.py:72-91` and `terminal_journal.py:478-512`. Terminal event validation exists in Python at `terminal_journal.py:404-454` and again in TypeScript at `terminalChannel.ts:47-59`, and the size bounds of 2 to 500 appear at `terminal_channels.py:37-38,49-51` and `terminalChannel.ts:38-45`.

The agent stream also has two paths. The SSE path starts at `frontend/src/hooks/useAgentStream.ts:127-133` calling `streamPrompt`, which posts to `/api/sessions/{id}/prompt` at `frontend/src/api/client.ts:514-570` with manual SSE line splitting at `:551-566` and `normalizeEvent` at `:503-512`. The backend handles `prompt_session` at `backend/src/yinshi/api/stream.py:771-773` with execution context resolved at `:630`, then `backend/src/yinshi/services/sidecar.py:39-136` provides newline-JSON transport with an 8 MiB message limit. The sidecar dispatches `query`, `resolve`, and `cancel` at `sidecar/src/sidecar.js:1203-1209`, shaping content blocks at `:244-250`.

The polled run journal path starts at `frontend/src/hooks/useAgentStream.ts:114-126` calling `startRuntimePrompt`. `frontend/src/runtime/promptStream.ts:30-249` posts `/runs`, polls `/runs/{id}/events/{seq}`, posts `/cancel`, and reuses `normalizeEvent` from `client.ts`. `backend/src/yinshi/api/prompt_runs.py:99-160` holds the routes and `backend/src/yinshi/services/prompt_journal.py:89-515` owns run lifecycle and sequenced batches, with `_default_prompt_executor:58` bridging to the same sidecar execution as the SSE path. Remaining sidecar hops match. Across the two stream paths, event normalization is shared, but transport, status enums, cancellation handling, and terminal-status handling are written twice. Compare `client.ts:514-575` with `promptStream.ts:9-249`. Two journals with near-identical sequenced-batch semantics also exist, in `prompt_journal.py` and `terminal_journal.py`.

## 5. Component dependency map

In the frontend, `App.tsx` depends on the pages and `components/Sidebar`. `pages/Session.tsx:19,67` depends on `runtime/useRuntimeResource`, which in turn depends on `runtime/runtimeRef`, `runtime/resolveRuntime`, and `runtime/runtimeTransport`. `runtime/runtimeTransport.ts` depends on `api/client`, `runner/encryptedRunnerClient`, and `runtime/encryptedUpload`. `runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts` depends on `crypto/noiseIk`, which loads noise-c.wasm, and on `api/client` for capability issuance. `hooks/useAgentStream.ts` depends on both `api/client.streamPrompt` and `runtime/promptStream`. `components/Sidebar.tsx` depends on the runtime modules, `runner/repositories`, and `api/client`. `api/client.ts` depends on `window.yinshiDesktop`, typed in `types/desktop.d.ts`.

In desktop, `main.ts` depends on sixteen local modules covering app control, supervision, launch configuration, secrets, credentials, disk status, the hosted gateway, hosted sessions and auth, security, shell policy, the auth callback listener, local repository import, automatic updates, and the IPC contract, all imported at `desktop/src/main.ts:21-48`. `preload.ts` depends on `desktopApi` channel names and exposes `window.yinshiDesktop` at `desktop/src/preload.ts:11-30`. `helperSupervisor` spawns the backend in desktop mode through `backend/src/yinshi/desktop_runtime.py`, and `sidecarSupervisor` spawns `sidecar/src/index.js` over `SIDECAR_SOCKET_PATH`.

In the backend, `main.py` depends on the `api` routers, middleware, `config`, and `db`. `api/stream.py` and `api/prompt_runs.py` depend on `services/prompt_journal`, which depends on `services/sidecar`. `api/terminal_channels.py` depends on `services/terminal_journal`, `services/workspace_runtime_paths`, `services/sidecar_runtime`, and `services/container`. `api/terminals.py` depends on `services/desktop_terminal` and talks to the sidecar socket directly. `api/runners.py` depends on `services/runners`, `services/runner_capabilities`, and `services/runner_relay`. `runner_agent.py` depends on `services/runner_agent_relay`, which depends on `services/runner_rpc`, `services/runner_noise_session`, and `services/runner_noise`, and it also depends on `runner_worker.py`, which imports `main.create_app` and `worker_runtime.WorkerHttpDispatcher`. `services/control_encryption` depends on `services/crypto`. In the sidecar, `index.js` depends on `sidecar.js`, which depends on `git_auth.js`, `git_askpass_client.js`, and `constants.js`, with no dependency on any other component.

Eight couplings deserve attention. An import cycle is broken only by a deferred import, because `backend/src/yinshi/runner_worker.py:264` imports `create_app` from `yinshi.main` inside a method body while `main.py` reaches worker code through routers and `worker_auth`. The backend also imports itself across a network boundary, since the BYOC runner runs a second full FastAPI app in-process at `runner_worker.py:288` and calls it over ASGI with no listening socket in `worker_runtime.py`, so one codebase acts as both control plane and remote worker, separated only by `app.state.mode`. Route knowledge is triplicated across three languages as described in section 3, and that is the highest-risk coupling in the repository. Two terminal subsystems and two agent-stream subsystems coexist with their own framing, and `api/terminals.py` and `api/terminal_channels.py` both talk to the same sidecar through separately written newline-JSON helpers. `api/client.ts` bypasses the runtime abstraction, because `DESKTOP_HOSTED_RUNNER_PATHS` at `client.ts:321-325` hard-codes three paths that must use the Electron bridge, so a fourth control-plane path added later would silently take the wrong transport. The default-runtime rule is written three times, at `runtimeRef.ts:62-67`, `Sidebar.tsx:172-174`, and `Settings.tsx:604-606` plus `:697`. Terminology drifts across layers, since the frontend says `local`, `hosted`, and `byoc`, the backend says `desktop`, `hosted`, and `worker`, and deployment material says runner, sidecar, and helper, with no file recording the mapping. The sidecar is the only fully decoupled component, knows nothing about runtimes, tenants, or Noise, and is a clean extraction boundary.

## Start here

Open `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts` first. Lines 10-17 define the `RuntimeRef` union that drives every frontend branch. Lines 46-206 hold the route-to-scope table duplicated in `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:132-215` and `desktop/src/hostedApiGateway.ts:16-170`. Lines 259-340 contain the dispatch that selects plain HTTP, the Electron bridge, or the Noise channel. Read `backend/src/yinshi/main.py:379-412` next for the backend mode split.

## Open questions

Is the RPC envelope `v: 2` at `encryptedRunnerClient.ts:483` intentional against `_REQUEST_KEYS_V1` at `runner_rpc.py:17`? Does the backend accept the `query` key that the frontend always sends, given its absence from `_REQUEST_KEYS_V1`? Is `api/terminals.py` still live or superseded by `api/terminal_channels.py`, since both are registered at `main.py:395-396`? Is `client.ts:streamPrompt` still live or superseded by `promptStream.ts`, since `useAgentStream.ts:127` still falls back to it without a runtime transport?

The Ed25519-signed claims are `scopes`, `token_id`, `transfer_id`, `expires_at`, `max_frame_bytes`, `max_session_bytes`, `initiator_public_key`, and `protocol`. The runner responder consumes them at `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_noise_session.py:178-225` and sends the handshake response payload `{"protocol":..., "transfer_id":...}` at `:216-224`. The frontend re-validates the same claim shape independently through the `RunnerCapabilityResponse` interface at `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:14-25` and `validateCapability` at `:118`, then parses the handshake reply at `:449-452`.

The relay framing layer adds a 16-byte UUID prefix that only the two Python endpoints understand. The hosted relay adds the prefix on client-to-runner traffic at `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_relay.py:266-283` as `uuid.UUID(transfer_id).bytes + ciphertext`, and strips it on runner-to-client traffic at `:298-330`. The runner side parses and re-adds the same prefix at `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_agent_relay.py:96-116`. Control messages are hand-built JSON strings rather than models. `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_relay.py:262-263` and `:328-330` emit `'{"transfer_id":"..","type":"close"}'`, parsed at `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_agent_relay.py:77-95,129-156`. The browser never sees the prefix. It sends bare ciphertext and expects the literal readiness string `'{"type":"ready"}'` at `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:441-443`.

The RPC envelope layer carries a version mismatch. The frontend request envelope sends `v: 2` at `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:472-484`, while the backend accepted key set is named `_REQUEST_KEYS_V1` at `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:17` and lacks `query`. Version and type checks run at `:83-100`. The response envelope is built at `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:313-325` and parsed independently at `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:495-500`. Size limits diverge by construction. The browser caps a request at 49152 bytes at `encryptedRunnerClient.ts:487-488`, the responder caps the frame from the capability at `runner_noise_session.py:265-271`, and the relay caps at `_RELAY_FRAME_BYTES_MAX` at `runner_relay.py:271`. Both the version-name mismatch and the missing `query` key are open risks.

Desktop encryption is a separate, unrelated scheme. `desktop/src/runtimeSecrets.ts:6-11` defines `RuntimeSecrets {version:1, secretKey, encryptionPepper, keyEncryptionKey}` and passes those values to the Python helper. The backend reads them through settings and derives keys with its own AES-GCM helpers at `backend/src/yinshi/services/crypto.py:48-231` and `backend/src/yinshi/services/control_encryption.py:11-30`. `desktop/src/diskEncryption.ts` only detects FileVault status through `detectFileVaultStatus`, imported at `desktop/src/main.ts:29`, and takes no part in the Noise protocol.

A protocol change requires coordinated edits in seventeen places. On the backend those are `services/runner_noise.py` for handshake primitives and length bounds, `services/runner_noise_session.py` for the prologue, capability binding, handshake reply, and frame limits, `services/runner_capabilities.py` for the protocol tag, claim schema, and scope set, `services/runner_rpc.py` for the envelope, version, and route-to-scope table, `services/runner_relay.py` for prefix framing, control JSON, and byte limits, `services/runner_agent_relay.py` for runner-side demux, `api/runner_relay.py` for the WebSocket endpoints, `api/runners.py` for capability issuance with the protocol echoed at `:198`, `runner_agent.py` for the relay client, registration, and key pinning, and `models.py` for `RunnerCapabilityCreateIn:370`, `RunnerCapabilityOut:393`, `RunnerRegisterIn:324`, and `RunnerNoiseKeyConfirmationIn:360`. On the frontend those are `crypto/noiseIk.ts`, `runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts`, `runtime/runtimeTransport.ts` for scope selection and the session byte budget at `:92`, `runtime/encryptedUpload.ts`, `runner/repositories.ts`, and `types/noise-c-wasm.d.ts`. Test mirrors in `frontend/src/crypto/noiseIk.test.ts`, `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.test.ts`, and the backend suites for those five services also change. Desktop is affected only when the `desktop/src/hostedApiGateway.ts` route allowlist must change, covered in section 3.

## 2. Type and schema duplication

There is no OpenAPI codegen. `frontend/package.json` has no `openapi` or generate script, and the backend serves `/openapi.json` only when `debug` is true, at `backend/src/yinshi/main.py:451`. Every API shape is hand-written twice, with Pydantic models in `backend/src/yinshi/models.py` and TypeScript interfaces in `frontend/src/api/client.ts`.

| Shape | Backend | Frontend |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Repo | `models.py:136` `RepoOut` | `client.ts:1` `Repo` |
| Workspace | `models.py:163` `WorkspaceOut` | `client.ts:178` `Workspace` |
| Session | `models.py:212` `SessionOut` | `client.ts:189` `SessionInfo` |
| Message | `models.py:224` `MessageOut` | `client.ts:199` `Message` |
| CloudRunner | `models.py:294` `CloudRunnerOut` | `client.ts:83` `CloudRunner` |
| Runner registration | `models.py:314` `CloudRunnerRegistrationOut` | `client.ts:101` `CloudRunnerRegistration` |
| Runner capability response | `models.py:393` `RunnerCapabilityOut` | `encryptedRunnerClient.ts:14` `RunnerCapabilityResponse` |
| Runner capability request | `models.py:370` `RunnerCapabilityCreateIn` | `encryptedRunnerClient.ts:27` `RunnerCapabilityRequest` |
| Provider descriptor | `models.py:448` | `client.ts:34` |
| Provider setup field | `models.py:439` | `client.ts:27` |
| Model descriptor | `models.py:460` | `client.ts:47` |
| Provider catalog | `models.py:475` | `client.ts:60` |
| Provider auth start | `models.py:483` | `client.ts:109` |
| Provider auth status | `models.py:495` | `client.ts:119` |
| Provider connection | `models.py:602` | `client.ts:66` |
| API key | `models.py:625` | `client.ts:19` |
| Pi config | `models.py:672` | `client.ts:131` |
| Pi command | `models.py:687` | `client.ts:146` |
| Pi config commands | `models.py:702` | `client.ts:153` |
| Pi package release | `models.py:713` | `client.ts:157` |
| Pi release notes | `models.py:724` | `client.ts:166` |
| Prompt request | `models.py:237` `WSPrompt` | inline at `frontend/src/runtime/promptStream.ts:42-49` and `client.ts:514-522` |

Four more duplications sit outside `models.py`. Terminal channel shapes appear at `backend/src/yinshi/api/terminal_channels.py:36-61` and again as hand validators at `frontend/src/runtime/terminalChannel.ts:11-59`, with the event-type set at `:4-9`. Prompt run shapes appear at `backend/src/yinshi/api/prompt_runs.py:99-160` and at `frontend/src/runtime/promptStream.ts:30-40`, with the run status enum duplicated at `promptStream.ts:9-28`. The SSE event union at `frontend/src/api/client.ts:453-502` mirrors sidecar content shaping at `sidecar/src/sidecar.js:244-250`. The desktop IPC contract in `desktop/src/desktopApi.ts` is duplicated for the renderer in `frontend/src/types/desktop.d.ts`, and the runtime secrets contract at `desktop/src/runtimeSecrets.ts:6-11` is mirrored by backend settings used in `backend/src/yinshi/config.py` and `services/crypto.py`.

## 3. Runtime abstraction and where the runtime decision is made

This is the key finding. Two orthogonal runtime axes exist, and they are not unified.

Axis A is the frontend `RuntimeRef.location`, with values `local`, `hosted`, and `byoc`. It is defined at `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:10-17`, and the unresolved variant sits at `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeRef.ts:6-13`. Axis B is the backend `AppMode`, with values `desktop`, `hosted`, and `worker`, selected in `backend/src/yinshi/main.py:415-457` through `create_app(mode=...)`. The names do not line up. Frontend `local` maps to backend `desktop`, frontend `byoc` maps to backend `worker` running inside `runner_agent`, and frontend `hosted` maps to backend `hosted`. Nothing in the code states or enforces that mapping.

The frontend branches on runtime in thirteen places. `frontend/src/runtime/useRuntimeResource.ts:42-51` is the canonical resolution, parsing the encoded ID, resolving the ref, and building the transport. In `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeRef.ts`, `defaultRuntimeRef` at `:62-67` returns `local` on desktop and `hosted` elsewhere, `runtimeResourceId` at `:69-83` encodes the runtime into the URL as `hosted.`, `local.`, or `byoc.<b64url>.`, and `parseRuntimeResourceId` at `:87-119` decodes it. `frontend/src/runtime/resolveRuntime.ts:20-45` resolves BYOC by fetching `/api/settings/runner` and requiring `noise_key_confirmed`. Inside `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts`, line range `259-273` selects `hostedApi` against `api` when the location is hosted and `window.yinshiDesktop` exists, `286-296` dispatches BYOC requests through the encrypted Noise channel, and `322-340` branches uploads three ways across BYOC encryption, the hosted bridge, and plain multipart. `frontend/src/runtime/promptStream.ts:174` sets the poll delay by runtime location. `frontend/src/api/client.ts:321-325, 374-378, 402-410` routes to the bridge using the hard-coded `DESKTOP_HOSTED_RUNNER_PATHS` set, which bypasses `RuntimeRef` entirely. `frontend/src/api/piCommandsCache.ts:22` namespaces the cache key by runtime. `frontend/src/components/Sidebar.tsx:172-247, 269, 514, 973, 1096, 1132, 1161` discovers and aggregates all three locations, and rebuilds the default runtime at `:172-174` instead of calling `defaultRuntimeRef`. `frontend/src/pages/Settings.tsx:604-606, 631-638, 697, 716, 757-764` holds a third open-coded copy of that same default-runtime rule at `:604-606` and `:697`.

The backend branches on mode in twelve places. `backend/src/yinshi/main.py:415-424` validates the mode inside `create_app`. Worker mode uses a distinct middleware stack and returns early at `:309-322`. Desktop mode injects `DesktopTenantMiddleware` with the fixed `desktop-local` tenant at `:344-352` and uses a different content security policy at `:361-363`. `_include_routes` at `:379-412` splits execution routers from control routers, so only hosted mode receives auth, runners, the relay, GitHub, and desktop devices. Hosted-only startup work runs at `:266`. The runner agent builds `create_app(mode="worker", ...)` in-process at `backend/src/yinshi/runner_worker.py:264-293`, and `WorkerHttpDispatcher` at `backend/src/yinshi/worker_runtime.py:29-40` asserts `app.state.mode == "worker"` before dispatching over ASGI with no socket. An execution-time branch at `backend/src/yinshi/api/terminal_channels.py:97-105` uses the settings socket and the host workspace path when no sidecar socket path exists, and otherwise remaps the path into the container. The mechanism behind that branch is `TenantSidecarContext` with a nullable `socket_path` at `backend/src/yinshi/services/sidecar_runtime.py:30-38`. A separate desktop terminal WebSocket proxy runs in parallel to the polling channel API at `backend/src/yinshi/api/terminals.py:188-274`. The route-to-scope table at `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:132-215` gates what a BYOC runtime may execute.

Desktop branches in four places. `desktop/src/main.ts:369` and `desktop/src/runtimeLaunchConfig.ts:120-160` set helper and sidecar socket paths and environment for the local runtime. `desktop/src/localRuntime.ts:15-30` asserts that helper and sidecar agree on `SIDECAR_SOCKET_PATH` before starting the pair. `desktop/src/hostedApiGateway.ts:16-170` allowlists the hosted API routes reachable through the bridge, which is the third copy of the route table. `desktop/src/helperSupervisor.ts` and `desktop/src/sidecarSupervisor.ts`, imported at `desktop/src/main.ts:32,48`, own local runtime process lifecycle.

The sidecar branches in three places, none of which concern runtime kind. `sidecar/src/sidecar.js:937` reads the socket path from `SIDECAR_SOCKET_PATH`, `:946` toggles dotenv on `SIDECAR_LOAD_DOTENV === "1"` while desktop sets `"0"` at `desktop/src/runtimeLaunchConfig.ts:158`, and `:1154-1210` holds one message-type dispatch table. The sidecar is runtime-agnostic.

The same URL surface is enumerated three times, in three languages, for three purposes. `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:132-215` performs authoritative server-side scope enforcement. `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:46-206` performs client-side scope selection for capability requests. `desktop/src/hostedApiGateway.ts:16-170` performs Electron bridge allowlisting. Any new API route requires edits in all three files plus the FastAPI router, and divergence here is a security-relevant defect class.

## 4. Terminal and agent-stream data paths

The polling terminal channel is the path required for BYOC, and it crosses twelve hops. `frontend/src/runtime/terminalChannel.ts:82` posts to `/api/workspaces/{id}/terminals` and polls `/events/{sequence}`, validating events at `:4-9,47-59`. `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts:286-296` wraps each BYOC call in a Noise RPC, and `frontend/src/runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts:441-520` performs the handshake and encrypted request. `backend/src/yinshi/api/runner_relay.py` with `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_relay.py:266-330` relays UUID-prefixed frames, and `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_agent_relay.py:96-116` demuxes to the per-transfer session. `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:71-325` parses the envelope, checks scope, and builds the response, then `backend/src/yinshi/worker_runtime.py:29` dispatches into the worker app over ASGI. `backend/src/yinshi/api/terminal_channels.py:121-250` holds the terminal routes and `:79-110` resolves workspace paths and the sidecar socket. `backend/src/yinshi/services/terminal_journal.py:85-512` writes newline-delimited JSON to the sidecar socket and buffers output into sequenced batches at `_append_event:404`, `_split_terminal_data:439`, and `_decode_message:512`. Finally `sidecar/src/sidecar.js:1184-1210` dispatches the terminal message types, and `:982-1082` spawns the pty, with `onData` emitting `terminal_data` at `:999-1003`, `onExit` emitting `terminal_exit` at `:1005-1012`, and ready emitting `terminal_ready` at `:1036-1042`.

A second terminal path exists as a direct WebSocket proxy. `backend/src/yinshi/api/terminals.py:273-274` exposes `/api/workspaces/{id}/terminal` with its own sidecar framing helpers at `_send_sidecar:72`, `_read_sidecar:81`, `_proxy_browser_to_sidecar:92`, `_proxy_sidecar_to_browser:169`, and `_run_desktop_terminal_proxy:188`. Workspace resolution runs at `backend/src/yinshi/services/desktop_terminal.py:37`. Sidecar newline-JSON framing therefore exists twice inside the backend, at `terminals.py:72-91` and `terminal_journal.py:478-512`. Terminal event validation exists in Python at `terminal_journal.py:404-454` and again in TypeScript at `terminalChannel.ts:47-59`, and the size bounds of 2 to 500 appear at `terminal_channels.py:37-38,49-51` and `terminalChannel.ts:38-45`.

The agent stream also has two paths. The SSE path starts at `frontend/src/hooks/useAgentStream.ts:127-133` calling `streamPrompt`, which posts to `/api/sessions/{id}/prompt` at `frontend/src/api/client.ts:514-570` with manual SSE line splitting at `:551-566` and `normalizeEvent` at `:503-512`. The backend handles `prompt_session` at `backend/src/yinshi/api/stream.py:771-773` with execution context resolved at `:630`, then `backend/src/yinshi/services/sidecar.py:39-136` provides newline-JSON transport with an 8 MiB message limit. The sidecar dispatches `query`, `resolve`, and `cancel` at `sidecar/src/sidecar.js:1203-1209`, shaping content blocks at `:244-250`.

The polled run journal path starts at `frontend/src/hooks/useAgentStream.ts:114-126` calling `startRuntimePrompt`. `frontend/src/runtime/promptStream.ts:30-249` posts `/runs`, polls `/runs/{id}/events/{seq}`, posts `/cancel`, and reuses `normalizeEvent` from `client.ts`. `backend/src/yinshi/api/prompt_runs.py:99-160` holds the routes and `backend/src/yinshi/services/prompt_journal.py:89-515` owns run lifecycle and sequenced batches, with `_default_prompt_executor:58` bridging to the same sidecar execution as the SSE path. Remaining sidecar hops match. Across the two stream paths, event normalization is shared, but transport, status enums, cancellation handling, and terminal-status handling are written twice. Compare `client.ts:514-575` with `promptStream.ts:9-249`. Two journals with near-identical sequenced-batch semantics also exist, in `prompt_journal.py` and `terminal_journal.py`.

## 5. Component dependency map

In the frontend, `App.tsx` depends on the pages and `components/Sidebar`. `pages/Session.tsx:19,67` depends on `runtime/useRuntimeResource`, which in turn depends on `runtime/runtimeRef`, `runtime/resolveRuntime`, and `runtime/runtimeTransport`. `runtime/runtimeTransport.ts` depends on `api/client`, `runner/encryptedRunnerClient`, and `runtime/encryptedUpload`. `runner/encryptedRunnerClient.ts` depends on `crypto/noiseIk`, which loads noise-c.wasm, and on `api/client` for capability issuance. `hooks/useAgentStream.ts` depends on both `api/client.streamPrompt` and `runtime/promptStream`. `components/Sidebar.tsx` depends on the runtime modules, `runner/repositories`, and `api/client`. `api/client.ts` depends on `window.yinshiDesktop`, typed in `types/desktop.d.ts`.

In desktop, `main.ts` depends on sixteen local modules covering app control, supervision, launch configuration, secrets, credentials, disk status, the hosted gateway, hosted sessions and auth, security, shell policy, the auth callback listener, local repository import, automatic updates, and the IPC contract, all imported at `desktop/src/main.ts:21-48`. `preload.ts` depends on `desktopApi` channel names and exposes `window.yinshiDesktop` at `desktop/src/preload.ts:11-30`. `helperSupervisor` spawns the backend in desktop mode through `backend/src/yinshi/desktop_runtime.py`, and `sidecarSupervisor` spawns `sidecar/src/index.js` over `SIDECAR_SOCKET_PATH`.

In the backend, `main.py` depends on the `api` routers, middleware, `config`, and `db`. `api/stream.py` and `api/prompt_runs.py` depend on `services/prompt_journal`, which depends on `services/sidecar`. `api/terminal_channels.py` depends on `services/terminal_journal`, `services/workspace_runtime_paths`, `services/sidecar_runtime`, and `services/container`. `api/terminals.py` depends on `services/desktop_terminal` and talks to the sidecar socket directly. `api/runners.py` depends on `services/runners`, `services/runner_capabilities`, and `services/runner_relay`. `runner_agent.py` depends on `services/runner_agent_relay`, which depends on `services/runner_rpc`, `services/runner_noise_session`, and `services/runner_noise`, and it also depends on `runner_worker.py`, which imports `main.create_app` and `worker_runtime.WorkerHttpDispatcher`. `services/control_encryption` depends on `services/crypto`. In the sidecar, `index.js` depends on `sidecar.js`, which depends on `git_auth.js`, `git_askpass_client.js`, and `constants.js`, with no dependency on any other component.

Eight couplings deserve attention. An import cycle is broken only by a deferred import, because `backend/src/yinshi/runner_worker.py:264` imports `create_app` from `yinshi.main` inside a method body while `main.py` reaches worker code through routers and `worker_auth`. The backend also imports itself across a network boundary, since the BYOC runner runs a second full FastAPI app in-process at `runner_worker.py:288` and calls it over ASGI with no listening socket in `worker_runtime.py`, so one codebase acts as both control plane and remote worker, separated only by `app.state.mode`. Route knowledge is triplicated across three languages as described in section 3, and that is the highest-risk coupling in the repository. Two terminal subsystems and two agent-stream subsystems coexist with their own framing, and `api/terminals.py` and `api/terminal_channels.py` both talk to the same sidecar through separately written newline-JSON helpers. `api/client.ts` bypasses the runtime abstraction, because `DESKTOP_HOSTED_RUNNER_PATHS` at `client.ts:321-325` hard-codes three paths that must use the Electron bridge, so a fourth control-plane path added later would silently take the wrong transport. The default-runtime rule is written three times, at `runtimeRef.ts:62-67`, `Sidebar.tsx:172-174`, and `Settings.tsx:604-606` plus `:697`. Terminology drifts across layers, since the frontend says `local`, `hosted`, and `byoc`, the backend says `desktop`, `hosted`, and `worker`, and deployment material says runner, sidecar, and helper, with no file recording the mapping. The sidecar is the only fully decoupled component, knows nothing about runtimes, tenants, or Noise, and is a clean extraction boundary.

## Start here

Open `frontend/src/runtime/runtimeTransport.ts` first. Lines 10-17 define the `RuntimeRef` union that drives every frontend branch. Lines 46-206 hold the route-to-scope table duplicated in `backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_rpc.py:132-215` and `desktop/src/hostedApiGateway.ts:16-170`. Lines 259-340 contain the dispatch that selects plain HTTP, the Electron bridge, or the Noise channel. Read `backend/src/yinshi/main.py:379-412` next for the backend mode split.

## Open questions

Is the RPC envelope `v: 2` at `encryptedRunnerClient.ts:483` intentional against `_REQUEST_KEYS_V1` at `runner_rpc.py:17`? Does the backend accept the `query` key that the frontend always sends, given its absence from `_REQUEST_KEYS_V1`? Is `api/terminals.py` still live or superseded by `api/terminal_channels.py`, since both are registered at `main.py:395-396`? Is `client.ts:streamPrompt` still live or superseded by `promptStream.ts`, since `useAgentStream.ts:127` still falls back to it without a runtime transport?
